item.title: Vikings tumble in the NFC playoff picture after loss
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 09: Carson Wentz #11 of the Minnesota Vikings hands the ball to Aaron Jones Sr. #33 against the Buffalo Bills during the first quarter of the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 09, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images When Week 9 started, the Minnesota Vikings found themselves in the #2 spot in the NFC playoff race, just behind the San Francisco 49ers. After their loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football, they’re now not only not on top of the NFC North, they’re not even in second place in the NFL’s best division, either. With every other team in the NFC North winning in Week 9, the Vikings are now in third place in the NFC North, behind both the Chicago Bears, who take over the division’s top spot, and the Detroit Lions, who have the same 6-2 record as the Vikings do but have the head-to-head tiebreaker of the Vikings thanks to their Week 8 victory. The 49ers. . .who the Vikings will see on Sunday Night Football in Mexico City in two weeks. . .continue to hold the top spot in the conference and the lone NFC bye with a 7-1 record. NFC North standings after Week 9 1. Chicago Bears (7-2) 2. Detroit Lions (6-2, win over MIN) 3. Minnesota Vikings (6-2, loss to DET) 7. Green Bay Packers (6-3) NFC playoff standings after the Vikings’ loss on MNF 1. San Francisco 49ers (7-1) 2. Chicago Bears (7-2) 3. New York Giants (5-2-1) 4. Carolina Panthers (3-5, 1-1 NFCS) 5. Detroit Lions (6-2, win over MIN) 6. Minnesota Vikings (6-2, loss to DET) 7. Green Bay Packers (6-3) 8. Seattle Seahawks (5-4, 2-1 NFCW) 9. Los Angeles Rams (5-4, 0-2 NFCW) 10. Dallas Cowboys (4-5) 11. New Orleans Saints (3-5, 0-1 NFCS) 12. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6, win over ATL, 3-3 NFC) 13. Atlanta Falcons (3-6, loss to TB, 3-3 NFC) 14. Arizona Cardinals (3-6, 2-5 NFC) 15. Washington Commanders (2-5-1) 16. Philadelphia Eagles (2-7) And yes, this means that, if the season ended today, the Vikings would have a first-round playoff date at MetLife Stadium against the New York Football Giants and their new starting quarterback. . .J.J. McCarthy. You know. . .not that anyone would notice, I’m sure. The Vikings have a date with the Packers at Lambeau Field next Sunday at noon Central Time in a game that will continue to shape the NFC playoff picture.

item.title: Seton Hall basketball beats Charlotte -- and finds a point guard
item.description: PHILADELPHIA – The Seton Hall basketball did more than win a game Monday night against a decent Charlotte team. The Pirates found a point guard. Junior Mihailo Petrovic came off the bench to spark an offense that had been stagnant through the season’s early going. The transfer from Illinois pushed all the right buttons as the Hall prevailed 68-62 before a small but vocal Pirate-dominated crowd at the Palestra, appropriately known as the cathedral of college basketball. Petrovic finished with 12 points, six assists, three steals and two turnovers in 30 minutes. He shot 4-of-6 from the field and it was clear his teammates’ confidence clearly rose with him at the controls. The ball moved better, the floor was spaced better, and the pick-and-roll consistently worked. In the ultimate compliment, Hall coach Shaheen Holloway started Petrovic in the second half over Del Jones – something the coach rarely does. It was recognition that he’s found something – if you have a point guard, you have a chance. And Seton Hall (3-0) now has a chance. Charlotte 49ers (2-1) was picked to finish fifth in the 13-team American Athletic Conference. There’s a chance this holds up as a Quad 2 victory and a neutral-court resume-booster. FIVE TAKEAWAYS 1. Devin Williams breaks out Terry Copeland’s foul trouble opened the door for Devin Williams, and the 6-foot-10 junior played his best game thus far, notching 16 points, four assists and two blocks in 22 minutes. Williams ran some nice pick-and-roll action and did a nice job drawing defenders to the paint before dishing to open teammates. He also set solid screens. He wasn’t perfect – he takes too many jump shots and should use his length to rebound better – but it was a clear step forward for the Florida Atlantic transfer. 2. Terry Copeland's foul trouble For the second straight game, the junior center picked up two quick fouls – and the first was a needless offensive foul away from the ball. The Pirates got through the first half without him, taking a 36-34 lead into the locker room, but at the start of the second half he picked up another foul when the Hall was on offense – a double-technical for shoving in transition. The Bergen Catholic grad is an essential piece for Seton Hall and if he’s going to foul, it has to be while defending the paint. With Copeland in trouble, Holloway made good on his pledge to get 7-footer Abdulai Fanta Kabba some run in the post. The 235-pound junior, who missed nearly two months of the preseason with a hamstring injury, looked rusty. He couldn’t finish and got beat on the defensive end. But he’s going to be needed, so consider those five minutes a down payment for later. 3. Defensive adjustments Charlotte has a big-time guard in Keyshuan Tillery, a sophomore who transferred from Cincinnati and came in averaging 26.5 points per game and shooting 56 percent from 3-point range. item.content:encoded: PHILADELPHIA – The Seton Hall basketball did more than win a game Monday night against a decent Charlotte team. The Pirates found a point guard. Junior Mihailo Petrovic came off the bench to spark an offense that had been stagnant through the season’s early going. The transfer from Illinois pushed all the right buttons as the Hall prevailed 68-62 before a small but vocal Pirate-dominated crowd at the Palestra, appropriately known as the cathedral of college basketball. Petrovic finished with 12 points, six assists, three steals and two turnovers in 30 minutes. He shot 4-of-6 from the field and it was clear his teammates’ confidence clearly rose with him at the controls. The ball moved better, the floor was spaced better, and the pick-and-roll consistently worked. In the ultimate compliment, Hall coach Shaheen Holloway started Petrovic in the second half over Del Jones – something the coach rarely does. It was recognition that he’s found something – if you have a point guard, you have a chance. And Seton Hall (3-0) now has a chance. Charlotte 49ers (2-1) was picked to finish fifth in the 13-team American Athletic Conference. There’s a chance this holds up as a Quad 2 victory and a neutral-court resume-booster. FIVE TAKEAWAYS 1. Devin Williams breaks out Terry Copeland’s foul trouble opened the door for Devin Williams, and the 6-foot-10 junior played his best game thus far, notching 16 points, four assists and two blocks in 22 minutes. Williams ran some nice pick-and-roll action and did a nice job drawing defenders to the paint before dishing to open teammates. He also set solid screens. He wasn’t perfect – he takes too many jump shots and should use his length to rebound better – but it was a clear step forward for the Florida Atlantic transfer. 2. Terry Copeland's foul trouble For the second straight game, the junior center picked up two quick fouls – and the first was a needless offensive foul away from the ball. The Pirates got through the first half without him, taking a 36-34 lead into the locker room, but at the start of the second half he picked up another foul when the Hall was on offense – a double-technical for shoving in transition. The Bergen Catholic grad is an essential piece for Seton Hall and if he’s going to foul, it has to be while defending the paint. With Copeland in trouble, Holloway made good on his pledge to get 7-footer Abdulai Fanta Kabba some run in the post. The 235-pound junior, who missed nearly two months of the preseason with a hamstring injury, looked rusty. He couldn’t finish and got beat on the defensive end. But he’s going to be needed, so consider those five minutes a down payment for later. 3. Defensive adjustments Charlotte has a big-time guard in Keyshuan Tillery, a sophomore who transferred from Cincinnati and came in averaging 26.5 points per game and shooting 56 percent from 3-point range. In the first half the Pirates had a tough time staying in front of him and also failed to cover the 3-point line as Charlotte shot 7-of-12 from deep. Personnel-wise, they gave up some defense to get the offense going. An understandable trade-off, but finding the balance is key. So it was notable that the defense improved in the second half, holding Charlotte to just 31 percent shooting. 4. The beauty of the Cathedral Even with a small crowd, the Palestra rocks. The acoustics are so good, the crowd so close to the court, that when 500 or so fans clad in Pirate blue chanted “Let’s go Pirates” or let out a full-throated cheer, it sounded like a roar. Monday at 9 p.m. is a tough time for fans in person (the game actually tipped at 9:20), so credit to the Pirate faithful who showed up took over the gym. There were very few Charlotte fans in the building, and the several hundred Penn fans who watched the Quakers dispatch Howard in the front end of the doubleheader left after that game. Seton Hall agreed to this matchup because of the appearance fee – the program needs revenue, as everyone knows – but its hardy fans made it a fun atmosphere. This was the program’s fourth contest in the Palestra this century. The Pirates beat La Salle in January 2004 and won a four-team tournament in 2007 by besting Navy and Virginia. 5. Acid test next Now comes the hard part – a trip to 18 th ranked Alabama Friday (9 p.m. tip). The Tide have beaten Sam Houston, Arkansas State and Oakland thus far and are averaging 102 points per game. It’s the front end of a home-and-home and a surefire Quad 1 opportunity. Jerry Carino has covered the New Jersey sports scene since 1996 and the college basketball beat since 2003. Contact him at jcarino@gannettnj.com . This article originally appeared on Asbury Park Press: Seton Hall basketball beats Charlotte -- and finds a point guard

item.title: Colts’ Jalen Travis out 2-4 weeks after suffering knee injury vs. Cowboys
item.description: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images Colts’ Jalen Travis out 2-4 weeks after suffering knee injury vs. Cowboys appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Indianapolis Colts face roster changes amid the NFL Trade Deadline coming Tuesday . But they’re dealing with a pivotal NFL injury too following the Dallas Cowboys loss involving tackle Jalen Travis. CBS Sports NFL insider Matt Zenitz dropped an update there on Monday evening. “Colts starting right tackle Jalen Travis is expected to miss 2-4 weeks due to a knee injury he suffered against the Cowboys yesterday, sources tell CBS Sports,” Zenitz posted on the social media website X, formerly known as Twitter. “The 2025 fourth-round draft pick has started all nine games for Indy this season.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Travis arrived via Iowa State and also played at Princeton in the Ivy League. He became the 127th overall pick of the ’25 draft. He immediately rose up the roster under coach Shane Steichen . But now the Colts have the trenches to address amid the Travis injury. Indianapolis may need to turn to the league’s trade market. Yet another dilemma involves keeping star running back Jonathan Taylor , as his name has grown popular ahead of the deadline. Indy faces the potential of possibly overpaying him too, which can cause a big salary cap dilemma for the franchise. It doesn’t help that the franchise dumped general manager Chris Ballard during the season . Ballard’s dismissal arrived following an embarrassing loss to the last place Tennessee Titans back on Oct. 18. So the Colts are also in the market of finding a new GM moving forward. Indianapolis sits at third in the AFC South with a dismal 2-7 overall record, including losing five straight games. Related: Packers’ perfect Jonathan Taylor trade offer to Colts before NFL trade deadline Related: Colts’ Shane Steichen keeps cards close to chest on trade deadline plans with rumors swirling

item.title: Tigers shortstop Kevin McGonigle reveals how he avoided the rookie wall on the way to ROTY win
item.description: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Tigers shortstop Kevin McGonigle reveals how he avoided the rookie wall on the way to ROTY win appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Detroit Tigers shortstop Kevin McGonigle explained how he avoided the rookie wall after winning the American League Rookie of the Year Award on Monday. McGonigle played 156 games and made 707 plate appearances in his first major league season. He handled that workload while splitting time between shortstop and third base, adjusting to the demands of two infield positions. The award followed an early show of confidence from Detroit. The Tigers signed McGonigle to an eight-year, $150 million extension in April, just weeks after his Opening Day debut. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) MLB Network shared McGonigle’s response Monday on X, formerly Twitter, capturing his explanation of how he stayed ready throughout his rookie season. “I think the biggest thing is the guys in the clubhouse. Just picking their brains. … So I think that’s what really helped me this year was just picking each other or everyone’s brain and just trying to get as much information and help as I could.” "Trying to find a routine that works best for me… that's what helped me this year, picking everyone's brain and getting as much help as I could." @tigers star Kevin McGonigle shares how he avoided the rookie wall on the way to winning AL Rookie of the Year! pic.twitter.com/nMlaaW3EXx — MLB Network (@MLBNetwork) November 10, 2026 The Tigers shortstop received 28 of 30 first-place votes, finishing ahead of Cleveland Guardians pitcher Parker Messick and Boston Red Sox pitcher Payton Tolle. Members of the Baseball Writers’ Association of America submitted their ballots before postseason play. He batted .278 with a .376 on-base percentage and .430 slugging percentage, finishing with 18 home runs, 72 RBIs, 97 runs and 12 stolen bases. McGonigle added 168 hits and 28 doubles while drawing 95 walks against 100 strikeouts. His patience at the plate helped him provide consistent offensive production across a full season. He became the sixth Tiger to win the award, joining Harvey Kuenn, Mark Fidrych, Lou Whitaker, Justin Verlander and Michael Fulmer. Detroit had not produced a winner since Fulmer in 2016 or a position-player winner since Whitaker in 1978. Under contract through 2034, McGonigle capped his debut season with an honor that reinforced Detroit’s early investment in his future. Related: Watch Tigers’ Kevin McGonigle’s live reaction to AL Rookie of the Year announcement

item.description: The IPL trade window has generated a lot of hype in the off-season, especially with franchises looking to strengthen their squads before the 2027 season. Apart from the mini-auction that generally steals all the limelight, trades among various teams can be equally important since it allows them to fill their gaps without engaging in a bidding war. MAKE YOUR BET WITH DAFABET AND GET UP TO 200% WELCOME BONUS With several prominent names already mentioned in the media, including Mumbai Indians captain Hardik Pandya, the trade period promises to be quite exciting. While the transfer period is still on, The Sporting News takes a look at all the IPL 2027 confirmed transfers and the biggest rumours making the rounds. Reports have claimed that both CSK and DC are showing interest in acquiring the Mumbai Indians captain. The CEO of CSK, Kasi Viswanathan, has outright denied that there are any talks of recruiting Pandya to their team. However, reports claim that the five-time champions are indeed trying to explore all possibilities and Delhi Capitals are also a possible destination for him. According to reports, Punjab Kings have emerged as the latest team in a race to sign the Mumbai Indians captain. They are reportedly closing in on a deal to sign Pandya. On November 5, Hardik Pandya shared a Diwali post on his social media, wearing a yellow shirt, which further sparked the rumours of the all-rounder joining CSK. item.title: Oilers’ Connor McDavid keeps bonkers streak alive after brutal Rangers blunder
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Oilers’ Connor McDavid keeps bonkers streak alive after brutal Rangers blunder appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Edmonton Oilers are getting incredible performances from Connor McDavid this year. He is on track to shatter records and is nearing the 50-point mark already. On Monday, he continued his unreal start to the year, though he did get some help from the New York Rangers. Rangers goaltender Dylan Garand attempted to clear the puck from behind his net. However, his clear attempt banked off the boards instead of rimming around them. McDavid found the puck and beat an out-of-position Garand to put the Oilers on the board. GARAND MAKES A MISTAKE GIVING IT RIGHT TO THE BEST PLAYER IN THE WORLD AND MCDAVID CONTINUES HIS 19 GAME POINT STREAK!!! 🔥🚨 pic.twitter.com/peOaYBj4Ay Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — B/R Open Ice (@BR_OpenIce) November 10, 2026 As mentioned in the video above, McDavid has now scored a point in 19 games straight games. In fact, he has not been held scoreless in any game this season. The Oilers superstar has 48 points on the year, and is two points off from an unreal run to 50 points. McDavid is on pace for more than 200 points this season . He is on a run that we have not seen in the modern NHL. And the Oilers are having a ton of success because of it. Edmonton entered this game with a record of 12-3-3 at this time. This places them atop the Pacific Division, slightly above the Vegas Golden Knights. Only the Minnesota Wild have more points than the Oilers at this point in the season. McDavid and the Oilers are looking to win the Stanley Cup this year. Edmonton has come close in recent seasons, but hasn’t been able to close the deal. If McDavid can continue this run of form, though, this could be the year the Stanley Cup returns north of the border. Related: Oilers coach Mike Babcock explains Jake Walman scratch vs. Rangers

item.title: Buffalo Bills stock report: Horns Up, Horns down in gritty win vs. Minnesota Vikings
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 09: Terrel Bernard #8 of the Buffalo Bills celebrates with teammates after intercepting a pass intended for Justin Jefferson #18 of the Minnesota Vikings during the third quarter of the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 09, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings played the kind of knock-down, drag-out football most of us anticipated tonight. The No. 1 defense in the NFL resides in Minnesota, and it was as-advertised throughout the evening. Defensive coordinator Brian Flores and his charges made life miserable for the league’s No. 1 scoring offense for most of the evening, but especially in the first half. Flores’ defense flustered, frustrated, beat, and battered Buffalo’s offense for most of the first 28 minutes of the contest, but Buffalo eventually broke through. Like the eponymous Rosie in my favorite AC/DC song, it wasn’t exactly pretty, but coming out of this game with a win wasn’t exactly small, either. For the Bills, emerging with a 23-6 victory tonight is a big statement. Buffalo’s defense looked great, and their offense did enough by moving the ball on an elite defensive unit to score enough points to win the game. Minnesota’s inept offense—combined with a strong effort from Buffalo’s much-maligned defense—gave Buffalo’s elite offense the time to find its footing. hat time was all Buffalo needed to come out with a win. There was plenty of good tonight, and there was enough bad to keep us talking throughout the week, as well. Here are our horns up and horns down for the Bills in this Monday night slug-fest. _____________________________________________________________________________ Horns Down: Austin Corbett Based on his play tonight, I don’t have to ask which Billy Joel album is Corbett’s favorite. While I also love Turnstiles , it’s not exactly how I want to see an offensive lineman perform. Yes, there is a reason why Corbett lost the preseason positional battle to Alec Anderson, but as a nine-year vet making his 79th career start, I didn’t expect him to be the guy consistently whiffing on blocks while quarterback Josh Allen ran for his life. Anderson was able to log a limited practice at the end of this past week, so he’s hopefully going to be able to play next week. I do wonder, though, if the Bills would consider using Tylan Grable at guard over Corbett in the future when both Dion Dawkins, who sat tonight with a rib injury, and Spencer Brown are both healthy. Horns Up: Greg Rousseau Groot was all over the offensive backfield at times, as he hit quarterback Carson Wentz three times, sacked him once, and whacked his throwing arm to cause an incomplete pass in the first half alone. Rousseau was a big problem in the passing game and the run game, as he consistently used his length to create issues for Minnesota’s offensive line. He even recovered a fumble on what was originally ruled an incomplete pass by Carso
item.content:encoded: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 09: Terrel Bernard #8 of the Buffalo Bills celebrates with teammates after intercepting a pass intended for Justin Jefferson #18 of the Minnesota Vikings during the third quarter of the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 09, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings played the kind of knock-down, drag-out football most of us anticipated tonight. The No. 1 defense in the NFL resides in Minnesota, and it was as-advertised throughout the evening. Defensive coordinator Brian Flores and his charges made life miserable for the league’s No. 1 scoring offense for most of the evening, but especially in the first half. Flores’ defense flustered, frustrated, beat, and battered Buffalo’s offense for most of the first 28 minutes of the contest, but Buffalo eventually broke through. Like the eponymous Rosie in my favorite AC/DC song, it wasn’t exactly pretty, but coming out of this game with a win wasn’t exactly small, either. For the Bills, emerging with a 23-6 victory tonight is a big statement. Buffalo’s defense looked great, and their offense did enough by moving the ball on an elite defensive unit to score enough points to win the game. Minnesota’s inept offense—combined with a strong effort from Buffalo’s much-maligned defense—gave Buffalo’s elite offense the time to find its footing. hat time was all Buffalo needed to come out with a win. There was plenty of good tonight, and there was enough bad to keep us talking throughout the week, as well. Here are our horns up and horns down for the Bills in this Monday night slug-fest. _____________________________________________________________________________ Horns Down: Austin Corbett Based on his play tonight, I don’t have to ask which Billy Joel album is Corbett’s favorite. While I also love Turnstiles , it’s not exactly how I want to see an offensive lineman perform. Yes, there is a reason why Corbett lost the preseason positional battle to Alec Anderson, but as a nine-year vet making his 79th career start, I didn’t expect him to be the guy consistently whiffing on blocks while quarterback Josh Allen ran for his life. Anderson was able to log a limited practice at the end of this past week, so he’s hopefully going to be able to play next week. I do wonder, though, if the Bills would consider using Tylan Grable at guard over Corbett in the future when both Dion Dawkins, who sat tonight with a rib injury, and Spencer Brown are both healthy. Horns Up: Greg Rousseau Groot was all over the offensive backfield at times, as he hit quarterback Carson Wentz three times, sacked him once, and whacked his throwing arm to cause an incomplete pass in the first half alone. Rousseau was a big problem in the passing game and the run game, as he consistently used his length to create issues for Minnesota’s offensive line. He even recovered a fumble on what was originally ruled an incomplete pass by Carson Wentz. He finished the game with just those first-half stats, but his presence was felt throughout the game. Horns Down: Early-Game Offensive Play Calls It took the Bills some time to settle into the game, as head coach and play-caller Joe Brady was far too predictable early. At one point, Buffalo had run the football on seven of nine first-downs. James Cook III is a great back, but when every first down is a handoff through the A-gap against a fantastic Minnesota defense, it becomes a little predictable. To his credit, Brady started to mix things up as the game progressed, and his calls diversified to include some spread looks—which really helped the Bills—as well as some better looks for Cook on second down runs. The adjustments helped Buffalo to move the ball against an elite defensive unit, putting up enough points for the game they were playing tonight. Horns Up: Jim Leonhard Kudos to the defensive boss, who was leading an awful unit through Buffalo’s first six games. Between tonight’s game and last week’s win over the Baltimore Ravens, Buffalo’s defense has looked like an entirely different unit. Granted, that success has come against two teams who were without their starting quarterbacks, but let’s not pretend that Carson Wentz is Joe Fagnano. Wentz might have looked like Fagnano for most of the evening, but part of that was thanks to the looks Buffalo’s defense gave him. Leonhard has done a nice job turning the tide for Buffalo’s stop unit over the last two weeks. If they can build on this, and maybe find some help on the trade market to supplement the group, things could be looking up. Horns Up: The Linebackers Dorian Williams and Terrel Bernard each made huge plays in the second half. Williams went up and made a big interception when he was one-on-one with tight end T.J. Hockenson, bringing an end to Minnesota’s first drive after the half. Then, after the Vikings had gashed Buffalo on the ground for four straight plays, Bernard undercut Justin Jefferson and intercepted Wentz off a play-action pass. Bernard had three pass breakups and Williams had one. Ultimately, both players looked good, as did rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr, who was flying around the ball on his snaps, as well. Bernard led the Bills in tackles, totaling six on the evening to go with the aforementioned pass breakups. Williams had three tackles, and Elarms-Orr had two on his ledger. Horns Up: Keleki Latu Any time you catch your first career touchdown, it’s a horns up from me. Latu did a great job staying alive on the scramble drill, and Josh Allen did Josh Allen things by finding him in the back of the end zone when basically any other normal human would have thrown the football away. It was a 25-yard score where Latu found himself wide open, and it was a huge score in what was mostly a field goal-fest. Latu even mixed it up as a blocker, looking more than capable of holding his own all night long. Horns Down: Staying On the Snap Count Five false start penalties. Sure, they’re on the road, and yes, Vikings fans were loud tonight. But, five? This is a continuing theme this season where little things that hint towards a team’s discipline—of lack thereof—show up. Buffalo has the talent to overcome it most of the time, but the Bills committed too many penalties again tonight. Pre-snap penalties are absolute killers. Horns Down: Tylan Grable Alright, maybe this is harsh, because stepping in to play left tackle against this Minnesota defense is no easy task. However, for any of us who thought that Grable could easily come in and replace Dion Dawkins, tonight was a bit of a reality check. Grable held his own for much of the game, but he did whiff entirely on linebacker Ivan Pace in the second half, leading to a sack on Josh Allen. As the game progressed, Grable and the rest of Buffalo’s offensive line was able to open holes for James Cook in the run game, but tonight’s performance didn’t show me that either Dawkins or Anderson should be anywhere but the starting lineup for the foreseeable future. Horns Up: James Cook III What a tough performance out of Cook tonight. He was an old-school workhorse in a game where the running game was an absolute necessity. This was just the fifth time in Cook’s career that he’s had more than 25 carries in a game, and just the second time in his career that he totaled 30 carries in a game. He handled the workload—and the punishment that came with it—beautifully. Cook totaled 107 yards and a game-sealing touchdown on his 31 carries. He dropped his only target, which came on Buffalo’s first possession of the game. Horns Up: Khalil Shakir Allen’s safety blanket was explosive in this one, coming up with big plays every time he touched the football. Whether it was on screen passes or crossing routes, Shakir made the most of his four targets, catching them all for 58 yards. It’s not the kind of stat line that impresses you in fantasy football, but against the NFL’s best defense, it’s the kind

item.title: ‘I hate this…’ – Doc Rivers clarifies Giannis Antetokounmpo takes after Miami star’s response
item.description: Credit: Megan Briggs/John Fisher via Getty Images Giannis Antetokounmpo expressed his disappointment about Doc Rivers’ comments recently, and his former coach has now clarified his stance. Doc Rivers made headlines a few days ago, when he criticised Giannis Antetokounmpo on a podcast appearance. The two were together in Milwaukee for over two years, but the Bucks failed to achieve anything of real significance during that era. Rivers suggested that the Greek Freak is not ‘easy to coach’ and made some comments about his playstyle which the Miami Heat star did not appreciate. Antetokounmpo was visibly disappointed when asked about it, and Rivers has now spoken for the first time since his interview blew up. Doc Rivers admits he hates the situation, apologises for being a ‘distraction’ Rivers has been in the NBA long enough to know better in terms of making such comments about a former superstar. Considering the Heat’s poor start to the season, his take was always going to be amplified. However, he does seem contrite about his role in starting the conversation. After his comments blew up the way they did, Rivers’ follow-up take came on Monday, and his words were shared by ESPN . “I was saying he was one of the most interesting guys,” Rivers said. “He makes unbelievable passes, but then at times, because of his force he plays at, it gets in the way of his feel. It was more of a compliment. I hate this and feel bad about it. I apologize for the distraction. I’m not trying to be one. “The point I was trying to make is whenever you have a great player, you have to fit the team around that great player,” Rivers told Andscape. “That is the point I was trying to make. It’s not always easy. It’s a compliment. I’ve been successful and unsuccessful at it.” Rivers also mentioned that he apologised to Giannis personally and that the 31-year-old responded positively to it. This should be the end of the discussion, although some may have enjoyed seeing it dragged out. Mutual respect is big in the world of sports, and Doc seems to have taken accountability for what his words have led to. item.title: Vikings’ Pathetic Offense Wastes Another Strong Defensive Effort Against Bills
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 9: Byron Murphy #7 of the Minnesota Vikings intercepts a pass during the first quarter of an NFL football game against the Buffalo Bills at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 9, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the second week in a row, the Minnesota Vikings’ defense held up for as long as they could against one of the better offensive units in the National Football League. And, for the second week in a row, the Minnesota offense did just about nothing to give them any sort of support at all. The Bills’ offense held the ball for over forty minutes on Monday night at U.S. Bank Stadium, and the Minnesota defense eventually just wore down as the Vikings fell to the Bills on Monday Night Football by a final score of 23-6 in Week 9. Things got off to a less-than-ideal start for the Vikings, as the Bills elected to receive the opening kickoff after winning the opening coin toss and got a big return from Greg Dortch, who took the ball all the way into Minnesota territory at the 36-yard line. But the Vikings’ defense got their first big stand of the night, as Josh Allen and the Bills’ offense went backward, culminating in a Dallas Turner sack of Allen on third down for a three-and-out and a punt that resulted in a touchback. The Vikings’ first offensive possession also resulted in a three-and-out, as Wentz’s first two passes went towards T.J. Hockenson, one a bad miss and a second short of the line to gain. Brett Thorson’s punt put the Bills at their own 33 to start their second possession of the night. The Bills put together a decent drive, with Allen converting on a couple of third-down throws to D.J. Moore and Khalil Shakir. Allen then converted another third down with his legs to put the Bills on the edge of the red zone, but Allen was called for intentional grounding on the next play thanks to Andrew Van Ginkel nearly dragging him down. After a screen got blown up to make it third and long, Allen tried to find D.J. Moore in the end zone, and instead found Byron Murphy for an interception, with Murphy getting a huge return to midfield for a big momentum shifter for the Minnesota defense. . @byronmurphy snatched it! 📺: @ESPNNFL pic.twitter.com/bsJ55mWnhA — Minnesota Vikings (@Vikings) November 10, 2026 But on the very next play, Wentz threw what was supposed to be a screen pass that was too high for Jefferson; it was first ruled incomplete and then, after review, changed to a lateral that was recovered by the Bills for another turnover that gave the ball right back to Buffalo in Minnesota territory. The Bills got themselves into position for a 39-yard field goal attempt for Tyler Bass, who connected to give the Bills a 3-0 lead with just under two minutes left in the first quarter. The Vikings barely avoided another disaster on the ensuing kickoff, as Myles Price got a nice return but had the ball popped out of his hands. Fortunately, the ball went directly to Ben Yur

Moore in the end zone, and instead found Byron Murphy for an interception, with Murphy getting a huge return to midfield for a big momentum shifter for the Minnesota defense. . @byronmurphy snatched it! 📺: @ESPNNFL pic.twitter.com/bsJ55mWnhA — Minnesota Vikings (@Vikings) November 10, 2026 But on the very next play, Wentz threw what was supposed to be a screen pass that was too high for Jefferson; it was first ruled incomplete and then, after review, changed to a lateral that was recovered by the Bills for another turnover that gave the ball right back to Buffalo in Minnesota territory. The Bills got themselves into position for a 39-yard field goal attempt for Tyler Bass, who connected to give the Bills a 3-0 lead with just under two minutes left in the first quarter. The Vikings barely avoided another disaster on the ensuing kickoff, as Myles Price got a nice return but had the ball popped out of his hands. Fortunately, the ball went directly to Ben Yurosek, who held on to set the Vikings’ offense up at their own 45-yard line. Unfortunately, the Vikings’ offense once again went three-and-out as Wentz continued to show a complete lack of accuracy on his passes, including one that Jefferson had to leap for that resulted in him going off the field slowly. After the Vikings punted it away, the Minnesota defense forced yet another three-and-out, with the ensuing Buffalo punt once again giving the Vikings good field position at their own 45-yard line as the first quarter came to an end. But the first possession of the second quarter resulted in yet another three-and-out for the Minnesota offense, and the Bills took over at their own 13 following yet another punt from Thorson. Minnesota’s defense, once again, forced a three-and-out as they continued to swarm Allen and gave him no time to get comfortable. After the punt, the Vikings actually got a first down. . .because of a defensive holding penalty on the Bills. But then, they got an actual first down on a pass from Wentz to T.J. Hockenson to move the ball into Buffalo territory. But that was followed by a sack of Wentz and more incompletions, and the Vikings punted again, with Tai Felton making a brilliant play to down the ball at the Buffalo 1-yard line. The Bills did pick up a first down on the ensuing possession, but a few plays later, Andrew Van Ginkel came flying around the edge to sack Allen and appeared to have forced a fumble that the Vikings recovered at the Buffalo 1-yard line to set up a first-and-goal. However, after review, the call was reversed. . .correctly. . .and it was ruled that Allen’s knee was down before the football came loose, resulting in a sack that put the ball at the 2 and forced another Buffalo punt. Myles Price took the punt to the Buffalo 34-yard line to set up the Vikings’ next drive. The Vikings didn’t gain many yards on the ensuing drive, but they did enough. . .by which we mean “didn’t go backwards”. . .but they did enough to give Will Reichard an opportunity from 43 yards out, and he put the ball between the uprights to tie things at 3-3 with four minutes left in the first half. The Bills took over and put together their best offensive drive of the night, marching into Minnesota territory, getting down to the Minnesota 25-yard line with less than a minute left. Then, Allen bought himself some time by rolling out to the right and found a wide-open Keleki Latu in the end zone for a 25-yard touchdown. It was the first touchdown of Latu’s career and gave the Bills a 10-3 lead with 44 seconds left in the first half. Minnesota got the ball back and Wentz, to his credit, managed to string a few completions together and got the Vikings into position for another Reichard try, this one from 53 yards out. Reichard split the uprights again, and the Vikings went into halftime trailing by a score of 10-6. The Vikings got the ball first to start the second half, and things got off to a decent start on a nice kick return by Price. A few plays later, Aaron Jones drew a 19-yard pass interference call to move the ball into Buffalo territory at the 37-yard line. However, on the next play, Wentz was looking for T.J. Hockenson and was intercepted by Bills linebacker Dorian Williams to put an end to what had been a promising drive. The Bills took over and put together another long, sustained drive into Minnesota territory. Allen’s pass on third-and-goal fell incomplete in the end zone, and they settled for another field goal from Bass, a 25-yarder that extended the Buffalo lead to 13-6 with six minutes remaining in the third quarter. The ensuing drive for the Vikings saw them get things going on the ground with three straight carries from Jordan Mason that picked up 24 yards and put the Vikings into Buffalo territory. Then, the Vikings asked Wentz to throw a pass, and he was promptly intercepted by Terrell Bernard to end the drive and give the ball back to the Bills at the Buffalo 34-yard line. Minnesota’s defense got another stop after the interception, with a touchback on the punt giving the Vikings the ball at their own 20. But, once again, Wentz and the Vikings couldn’t manage even one first down as they punted it away again after a three-and-out. The Bills got the ball back and pushed into Minnesota territory at the 38, where they had a 3rd-and-1. Allen pushed forward on a quarterback sneak and appeared to have the line to gain, but Kevin O’Connell challenged the spot and won to make it 4th-and-inches. Allen tried another sneak, and after initially being ruled short, Allen got the first down. Shortly after that, James Cook went into the end zone from five yards out for a score that, essentially, sealed the deal for the Bills, putting them ahead 20-6 with six minutes left in regulation. The Vikings got the ball back after the Cook touchdown and went four-and-out, going for it on a fourth down and failing when a Wentz pass for Jefferson fell incomplete. The Bills took over an

item.title: WTA made a mistake releasing ‘Behind the Scenes’ photo shoot video for 2026 WTA Finals
item.description: Tennis fans are still talking about the 2026 WTA Finals photo shoot for all the wrong reasons. Gone from previous years was the group shot with the players wearing elegant formal wear. This year gave us individual photos and fashion misses. The WTA should have left well enough alone by not mentioning the photo shoot ever again, but in its infinite tone-deaf wisdom, five days after the photos were taken, a social media “behind the scenes” video was released. MORE: WTA Finals Indian Wells drops ‘Final Swing’ signature cocktail First words of video explain exactly what went wrong Nov 9, 2026; Indian Wells, CA, USA; Aryna Sabalenka serves as she defeated Karolina Muchova (not pictured) in her round 2 match during the WTA Finals at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The making of a look 🤩 Take a dive Behind the Scenes of our iconic photoshoot. See the journey from start to finish 📺 https://t.co/TX8rOx5Enn #FAGEWTAFinals | #TheUltimateStage https://t.co/ri7HDNFes0 — wta (@WTA) November 10, 2026 The person who speaks first, stands near a rack of clothes, and says, “We have a lot of stuff.” That was precisely the problem. There was too much stuff, passing as designer clothing, that the athletes were wearing. Here are the FINAL PORTRAITS of all 8 women in the WTA Finals! https://t.co/Pg3msalTEX — Liza (@Liza1358335) November 6, 2026 A social media post best described it: “WTA finals shoot styling looks like they threw 200 pieces of clothing in the air and told them all to run under it” Another person appopriately compared Mirra Andreeva’s look to the infamous Friends episode when Joey wears all of Chandler’s clothes. @tennisbish Mirra looking like Joey 😭 https://t.co/C9DhCm2jGJ — ggp (@Gabriel05429660) November 6, 2026 MORE: Wimbledon doubles champ Kristina Mladenovic urges WTA Finals to go back to glamorous group photo Kristina Mladenovic was the only brave one to speak out Mladenovic told her followers that she wore the only good outfit in her suitcase because she did not like the “vision/styling” of the shoot. She also encouraged the WTA to go back to the iconic glam shoots of the past. Hopefully the WTA takes her advice. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Brady ends association with Birmingham City
item.description: Brady brought an end to his illustrious NFL career in 2023 [Getty Images] NFL legend Tom Brady has ended his association with top-of-the-table Championship side Birmingham City. The record seven-time Super Bowl champion became a minority owner in the St Andrew's club in August 2023 when he "entered a partnership" with club owners Knighthead Capital Management LLC. Part of Brady's role involved him being chairman of an advisory board at Birmingham, with the club saying he would be "both investing [as well as] committing his time and extensive expertise" following his arrival. However, the Blues announced his exit with a statement headlined 'Tom Brady departure'. They added: "Birmingham City Football Club expresses its sincere gratitude to Tom Brady for his involvement with and unwavering support for the club over the last three years. "It was truly amazing to have someone with Tom's experience and passion associated with the club, and the club looks forward to continuing to build on that foundation from the training ground to the Birmingham community." Former quarterback Brady, a three-time NFL most valuable player, retired in February 2023 after 23 seasons in the NFL, having won six Super Bowl rings with the New England Patriots and one with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Following the end of his playing career, he acquired a stake in the Las Vegas Raiders while also becoming part of the ownership group of the WNBA's Las Vegas Aces. On top of that, Brady's commitments include him being a lead NFL analyst for Fox Sports. He leaves with Birmingham top of the Championship on goal difference with 29 points after 15 games. 'I feel kind of old' - Patriots unveil 12ft Brady statue Follow your club with BBC Sport Listen to the latest Football Daily podcast Get football news sent straight to your phone

item.title: Lions move up in NGC playoff picture following Vikings loss
item.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 1: Jared Goff #16 of the Detroit Lions looks to pass during the second quarter against the Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field on November 1, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions got some help in their playoff quest on Monday night from the Buffalo Bills. The Minnesota Vikings lost, falling from second in the NFC to sixth and the Lions move up to fifth from sixth because of it. Detroit is now a half-game behind the Chicago Bears for first place in the NFC North and second place in the NFC. The Bears won on Sunday night to hold onto that slight edge. The Green Bay Packers also won and are nipping at the heels for the division. All four NFC North teams are in the playoffs as of right now. NFC playoff standings after the Vikings’ loss on MNF 1. item.title: LSU basketball's bench players shine in win over Louisiana Tech
item.description: BATON ROUGE — Efficiency and consistency have been two buzzwords for Will Wade and LSU basketball to start the 2026-27 season. The Tigers showcased signs of both in their dominating 90-50 win over Louisiana Tech on Monday, Nov. 9 inside the comforts of Pete Maravich Assembly Center. They finished shooting 32% from the field as a team while holding the Bulldogs to a season-low of 50 points. In the process of finding more efficiency and consistency, LSU may have also found its bench weapons in center Michael Ruzic and guard Abdi Bashir Jr. “Look we’ve got eight starters, all those guys can start,” Wade said. “Those guys can all start for a lot of teams. I thought Divine’s (Ugochukwu) a great finisher. Abdi obviously, made four 3s tonight. Ruzic was his normal self. Those guys gave us 40 points, which was huge, but we expect that because we’ve got a lot of depth.” Ruzic and Bashir were the first two players to enter the game off the bench for the Tigers and the duo immediately got to work. LSU’s deep ball threat off the bench Bashir showcased why he’s one of the team’s deep-ball threats, draining a trey in his first minute on the floor. The 6-foot-5 and 175-pounder would go on to lead the Tigers’ three-point shooting, draining four 3s. Bashir ended the night with 16 points along with a rebound and an assist. Having a sharpshooter like Bashir come off the bench will be key for Wade throughout the season, especially if a starter is in a slump. That’s somewhat the case to start the season with LSU’s starting shooting guard Skyy Clark going 0-for-14 from deep before draining his first trey Monday against Tech. “We’re a good three-point shooting team,” Bashir said. “Obviously, we're so dominant in the paint that we don’t need to rely on 3s, but when we get open looks, we got guys that can knock them down. I believe in Skyy more than anybody else on the team to knock them down. And it’s only a matter of time before he goes like 6 for 6 from deep in one game.” So far this season, Bashir is leading the Tigers with 11 made 3-pointers, and finished the Tech contest shooting close to 40% from deep. item.title: Browns defense has big day from Carson Schwesinger, but yields two late TDs
item.description: NEW ORLEANS, LA - NOVEMBER 8: Jordyn Tyson #0 of the New Orleans Saints dives forward past Carson Schwesinger #49 of the Cleveland Browns during the second half of a game at Caesars Superdome on November 8, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Browns’ defense forced the Saints into some mistakes, living on the edge at times. It’s still frustrating to see them hold New Orleans without a touchdown for much of the game, only to allow back-to-back touchdowns in the final minute and then in overtime. Below, we analyze the snap counts and stats on defense for the Cleveland Browns ’ Week 9 game against the New Orleans Saints. Defensive Line Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats DL Mason Graham 52 69% 1 tackle, 3 assists (4 combined). 1 QH. DL Isaiah McGuire 51 68% 3 assists (3 combined). DL Jared Verse 43 57% 2 assists (2 combined). DL Mike Hall 38 51% 1 tackle, 1 assist (2 combined). 1 sack, 1 TFL, 1 QH. DL Sam Kamara 36 48% 1 tackle, 2 assists (3 combined). DL Sam Williams 28 37% 1 QH, 1 pass defended. DL Derek Barnett 28 37% 1 assist (1 combined). DL Adin Huntington 23 31% No stats registered. Maliek Collins was out this week, and Cleveland has turned what should’ve been a strength at defensive tackle into a bit of a weakness lately. The run defense just isn’t there. On a day where Myles Garrett finally returned for the Rams and had three sacks, I got to watch Jared Verse have a chance at a sack right in front of him, and not come up with it. Verse again ranked toward the bottom of the PFF grades for defenders, and also had an offsides penalty early on. Hat tip to Adin Huntington — even though he didn’t log a stat on defense, he forced a fumble on a punt return. Linebacker Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats LB Carson Schwesinger 75 100% 10 tackles, 5 assists (15 combined). 2 sacks, 2 TFL, 2 QH, 1 forced fumble. LB Quincy Williams 68 91% 5 tackles, 2 assists (7 combined). A week after Carson Schwesinger had one of his worst games, he came back with one of his best. He registered 15 tackles and had 2 sacks (both were chasing down Tyler Shough when he tried to take off). He also forced a big fumble at the goal line on Jordyn Tyson , and was the Browns’ highest-graded defender by PFF with a grade of 90.8. Cornerback Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats CB Tyson Campbell 75 100% 4 tackles, 3 assists (7 combined). 1 fumble recovery. CB Denzel Ward 73 97% 2 tackles, 3 assists (5 combined). 1 pass defended. CB Myles Harden 48 64% 4 tackles, 1 assist (5 combined). 2 sacks, 2 TFL, 2 QH, 1 pass defended. CB Mekhi Blackmon 5 7% 1 tackle (1 combined). item.title: Midterm report card grades for all 32 NFL teams
item.description: The NFL has reached the halfway point of the 2026 season. For some teams, like the Los Angeles Chargers, this one can't end soon enough. A team that won 11 games in 2025 is 0-8. Winless heading into a Monday night game in Baltimore. The frosty Joe Buck-Troy Aikman relationship needs to provide more tension than the game between floundering squads. But getting back the NFL season after nine weeks, a time to dish midterm grades. Arizona Cardinals The Cardinals won two games at SoFi Stadium in the first half and another at Dallas. They have gone through Gardner Minshew II at QB, now injured, after sending Jacoby Brissett to third string before banishing him to Baltimore. They are in an impossible division and getting better is a challenge. Grade: C- Atlanta Falcons The Dirty Birds sit last in the horrible NFC South. They have shown moments of improvement only to slip into the abyss. They have lost two in a row heading into the second half and are 1-4 at home. Michael Penix Jr. showed promise. Showing isnt't doing. Grade: D Baltimore Ravens A team that was once 4-1 is now 4-5. It has gone through Lamar Jackson, Jacoby Brissett, and Joe Fagnano at quarterback. Next man up appears to be Jacoby Brissett, acquired from Arizona. The Ravens have been outscored by 47 points over nine games. The defense, supposed to be a strength, is vulnerable under first-year coach Jesse Minter. Not a good look. Will Brissett save the season? Grade: D + Buffalo Bills We have seen this script many times. The Bills look like a powerhouse in the regular season. Will this year be different and could they earn their first ring? The first half has been promising, minus the loss to the Patriots. Strong offense, solid defense. Grade: A Carolina Panthers The Panthers are fortunate to be in the NFC South. That way a 3-5 record keeps you in the playoff hunt in the NFC South. This was a team that made the playoffs as division champs last year and looked to be on the improve. That hasn't happened. A loss at home to the Broncos concluded the first half on a three-game losing streak. Grade: D- Chicago Bears If the Bears can win a game with more turnovers than Chicago's famed Mindy's Bakery, anything is possible. Look for Caleb Williams not to throw four picks in a game again, maybe in his career. The Jeffery Simmons acquisition looks genius. Grade: A - Cincinnati Bengals Joe Burrow has delivered and the defense has been acceptable. A team that usually struggles early is now 6-2 heading into the second half of the season. They also have won four out of five games on the road, which is a nice accomplishment. Could this be the year the Bengals are for real? Grade: A Cleveland Browns The Browns were 5-2. They are now 5-4 after losing to the Steelers, which is understandable, and the Saints, which isn't. That said the loss to New Orleans happened with Shedeur Sanders at QB for an injured Deshaun Watson. The fast start created excitement in Cleveland. Will it be doused with another losing stre

Grade: A - Cincinnati Bengals Joe Burrow has delivered and the defense has been acceptable. A team that usually struggles early is now 6-2 heading into the second half of the season. They also have won four out of five games on the road, which is a nice accomplishment. Could this be the year the Bengals are for real? Grade: A Cleveland Browns The Browns were 5-2. They are now 5-4 after losing to the Steelers, which is understandable, and the Saints, which isn't. That said the loss to New Orleans happened with Shedeur Sanders at QB for an injured Deshaun Watson. The fast start created excitement in Cleveland. Will it be doused with another losing stretch? Grade: B- Dallas Cowboys The Cowboys are 4-5 after downing a weak Indianapolis Colts team ... in the final minute. This is the usual song and dance for Dallas. Great expectations, even more surprising losses. The offense is powerful. The defense can be had by the worst of teams. Hard to believe they are under .500 and chasing the Giants. Grade: C- Denver Broncos For a team that has heard all sorts of criticism for its offensive woes, the Broncos are 7-2 and on top of the AFC West. Sean Payton made the only move, taking back play-calling responsibilities. What might be most remarkable is the Broncos are where they are despite outscoring opponents by only 12 points. Grade: B Detroit Lions For all the problems and troubles that the Lions seem to bring upon themselves with poor defense, they are 6-2. It is hard to believe that this franchise often beset by losing has such a good record. Almost unnoticed. They even managed to win a game scoring less than 20 points by thwarting the inept Miami offense. Grade: B Green Bay Packers How would you like to be 6-3 and last in your division? After a slow start, that is where Green Bay is in the NFC North. The Packers have vastly improved and figure to have a say in what goes on in the NFC throughout the rest of the season and playoffs. Grade: B Houston Texans Big whoop, the Texans defeated the winless Chargers to improve to 3-5. Nothing to brag about for a team that was regarded to have one of -- if not the -- best defenses in the league. They would have to win out to match last year's record. As crazy as it sounds for a team with such a bad mark, it isn't impossible. The schedule is favorable. Grade: D Indianapolis Colts This team is so far from the one that had a great first half last season. It has traded top players and who knows what others can move before the trade deadline. They actually were ahead of the Cowboys before allowing a touchdown in the final minute to complete the first half a putrid 2-7. Shane Steichen has to be on the hot seat. Grade: F Jacksonville Jaguars Don't look now but the Jags are a powerhouse. They cleaned the Falcons' clock in Madrid to finish the first half at 6-2. Most impressive is this stat: Jacksonville has outscored opponents by 108 points. The defense is allowing all of 15 points per game and added more players the day before the trade deadline. Trevor Lawrence has blossomed. Grade: A Kansas City Chiefs They are back. A 6-2 first half. They caught a soft opponent in Week 9, toppling the Jets to end the two-game losing streak. The Chiefs' dynasty was dismissed after last season's poor result. Feels like that was premature. Grade: A- Las Vegas Raiders The Raiders came out of gate with three wins, lost four in a row, then beat the Jets. Back to reality against the 49ers. Interesting to see if Fernando Mendoza becomes the starter at some point. Guess he is learning watching Kirk Cousins beat teams he should and lose to those he should. Grade: C- Los Angeles Chargers Horrific. Embarrassing. An 0-8 record after winning 11 games in 2025. Will Jim Harbaugh feel any heat from what is looking like as stunningly bad result in 2026. One fun nugget: The last time the Chargers were 0-8 was the year 2000. One of the quarterback on that roster was ... Jim Harbaugh. Los Angeles Rams A 2-4 start has become a 5-4 record. Nothing awesome in the victories, doing enough to get by as they did against the Commanders in Week 9. Matthew Stafford is a year older and not looking like 2025 MVP season. They finally got Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett on the field against Washington. Guess it is a good thing to be where they are with the issues they have faced due to injuries. And now they lose Puka Nacua, likely to IR. Grade: C+ Miami Dolphins They have been outscored by 74 points and only beat the New York. Jeff Hafley's team is trying and the defense is getting better. Malik Willis was a reach at quarterback and the offense is paying for it. Grade: D Minnesota Vikings The defense is an A+. The offense is a C-. That is how you wind up with this. Grade: B New York Giants The John Harbaugh hire has led to a 5-2-1 first half. They Giants have a huge lead in the NFC East because the other three teams are awful. They have done this without Jaxson Dart, going to Jameis Winston and J.J. McCarthy. They have also only outscored opponents by 10 points. If they win the division, this feels like the second team you would love to play in the playoffs. With the first being the NFC South champ. Grade: B New York Jets Not sure what Woody Johnson is waiting for because looking to another head coach. The Jets are 2-7 and only beat the Browns and Titans. They have lost to the Raiders, Dolphins, and have the Bills next. Oh, everyone should be excited for the Nov. 22 game at SoFi against the Chargers. Grade: F Philadelphia Eagles They are far more likely to finish last in the NFC East than any other team, which is stunning. The E

item.title: Michigan’s Kyle Whittingham makes head-scratching NIL comments
item.description: Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham watches a play against Indiana during the first half at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026. Michigan’s Kyle Whittingham makes head-scratching NIL comments appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Michigan football is 5-4 after an embarrassing 15-6 loss at the hands of the 3-6 Michigan State Spartans in Ann Arbor that caused coach Kyle Whittingham to think twice about potentially playing backup QB Bryce Underwood . Whittingham fired former offensive coordinator Jason Beck after the game, announcing that the Wolverines would conduct a nationwide search for the team’s play-caller. Offensive line coach Jim Harding has taken over Beck’s duties and will be tasked with outscoring coach Dan Lanning’s high-flying Oregon Ducks in Week 11 at Autzen Stadium in Eugene, Oregon, a job made all the more difficult by Dylan Raiola and the rest of his teammates. Whittingham shared controversial comments about the the Ducks’ Name, Image and Likeness (NIL) expenditures prior to the game, which many Wolverines fans took issue with on social media. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Outstanding football coach, defensive-minded coach. That’s his background, but tireless recruiter. He really does a great job recruiting. It doesn’t hurt that you have $50+ million at your disposal, in essence, (to) outbid everybody. Not everybody, but a lot of people. But that’s not his fault. That’s a credit. I mean, that’s a credit to their program and their dedication and desire to win and the support they have.” Whittingham will attempt to lead his Wolverines to their first win over the Ducks since 1973 after they lost the last three meetings. The all-time series is tied at three wins each. Whittingham has kept his job despite consistent calls from fans, including Barstool Sports’ Dave Portnoy , to be fired. His comments on NIL expenditures seemed to point back at his own team’s budget, causing fans to scratch their heads ahead of Week 11’s 3:30 p.m. kickoff in Eugene. Related: Oregon HC Dan Lanning makes tough Teitum Tuioti injury update before Michigan clash Related: Kentucky TE accuses Tennessee of pumping fake crowd noise into Neyland Stadium

item.title: Tide Rides Hot Shooting To 109-68 Victory
item.description: The Alabama Crimson Tide improved to 3-0 on the young season Monday night by destroying Oakland 109-68 in Coleman Coliseum. Bama shot 63% from the field, and 52% from three. The Tide made 14 out of 15 two point attempts. The Golden Grizzlies fell to 0-4. The Grizzles reside in Michigan, not in California. Aden Holloway made his season debut after serving a five game suspension- which included the three exhibition games. Holloway was joined in the starting lineup with Amari Allen, London Jemison, Drew Fielder, and Brandon Garrison. Oakland coach Greg Kampe sent out Nassim Mashhour, Chris Fields, Jr., William Kassi, Warren Marshall IV, and Belal El Shakery. Unlike the first two games of the year, the Tide came out hot. Allen hit a pair of three’s in the first two minutes. With 15:57 left Bama led 10-5. Keitenn Bristow scored twice on alley-oops before Qayden Samuels hit back to back three pointers. Jemsion hit two from deep followed by long range makes from Tarris Bouie and Cole Cloer. With six minutes left the Tide led 40-18. Holloway found his stroke knocking down a pair long balls, one from at least 35 feet. Jemison made his third in three tries and Bama took a 59-26 lead into the locker room. The Tide sent out the same starters for the second stanza, and things didn’t change. Fiedler hit a three pointer from the corner to start things followed by two more from Jemison wrapped around another one from Holloway. With 16:43 remaining the scored stood at 70-35. The barrage from deep continued with Jemison, Holloway, and Fielder remaining hot. Freshman Jaxon Richardson made his first career three pointer, and Bouie added another. A Bouie basket in the paint put the Tide in triple digits for a 100-65 lead with 1:53 left. Freshman point guard Anderson Diaz finished off the scoring with three straight three pointers and the Tide covered the 38.5 point line with the resounding 109-68 victory. In the second half Bama shot 19-32 for 59%, 13-25 for 52% from three, and made 7-8 at the free throw line. The Tide finished with 31 rebounds- 7 offensive, 30 assists, 10 blocks, 10 steals, and committed 12 turnovers. Jemison had a perfect shooting night, scoring 20 points on 7-7 shooting, including 6-6 from three point range. All of his long range shots were from the corner. Allen had another strong night with 14 points on 4-5 shooting, 3-4 from three, Holloway was next with 12 points on 4-8 from deep, with two rebounds, and two assists. Bouie was also in double figures with 10 points and added two rebounds and one block. Fielder added eight points, four rebounds, three assists, one block, and a steal. Garrison followed his double-double from Friday with nine points on 4-4 shooting with two blocks, and one steal and one assist. Diaz finished with nine points with four assists, and three steals. A Bouie basket in the paint put the Tide in triple digits for a 100-65 lead with 1:53 left. Freshman point guard Anderson Diaz finished off the scoring with three straight three pointers and the Tide covered the 38.5 point line with the resounding 109-68 victory. In the second half Bama shot 19-32 for 59%, 13-25 for 52% from three, and made 7-8 at the free throw line. The Tide finished with 31 rebounds- 7 offensive, 30 assists, 10 blocks, 10 steals, and committed 12 turnovers. Jemison had a perfect shooting night, scoring 20 points on 7-7 shooting, including 6-6 from three point range. All of his long range shots were from the corner. Allen had another strong night with 14 points on 4-5 shooting, 3-4 from three, Holloway was next with 12 points on 4-8 from deep, with two rebounds, and two assists. Bouie was also in double figures with 10 points and added two rebounds and one block. Fielder added eight points, four rebounds, three assists, one block, and a steal. Garrison followed his double-double from Friday with nine points on 4-4 shooting with two blocks, and one steal and one assist. Diaz finished with nine points with four assists, and three steals. Bristow continues to do a little of everything with nine points, three rebounds, three blocks, one steal, and one assist. Cole Cloer, who is supposed to be a sharp shooter, continued to struggle, making only 1-6 from deep, but added six rebounds, with three assists, and a sweet backwards dunk where he showed his hops. Oakland improved in the second half, shooting 15-33 for 45%, but only 1-7 from deep. The Grizzles were 8-12 at the charity stripe in the half. Overall the visitors finished 23-66 for 35%, 3-18 for 17% from three, and 19-25 for 70% on free throws. The Grizzlies had 37 rebounds, 21 offensively, eight assists, nine steals, blocked zero hots, and turnover it over 15 times. Masshour scored 18 points to lead the team and grabbed five rebounds. Fields Jr, had a double-double with 15 points and 13 rebounds with three assists and two steals. Seven of Fields boards were offensive. This was a fun game for the team and fans. 14 players played, Jamarion Fleming- Davis was held out with injury, and 11 saw 14 minutes or more of action. Garrison led the team with 22 minutes and Holloway followed with 21. Twelve different players notched at least one assist in the game. Once again Oats was disappointed in the rebounding with the Golden Grizzlies winning the battle of the boards. The Tide head man was most concerned the 21 offensive rebounds grabbed by the smaller visitors. In the Tide’s defense when you shoots 14-15 from two point range and 24-46 from three point range, you don’t leave yourself many offensive rebounding opportunities. However the Grizzlers were relentless on their end and often had multiple shots because of their work on that end. The Tide is a deep team with a lot of weapons. When the schedule toughens up, Oats will have to figure out how to dole out minutes. If a player doesn’t commit to playing defense and rebounding they will be grabbing some pine next to the coaching staff. Also given the teams propensity for injuries over the last several years, there is a good chance all players won’t be available every game. Next up is a Friday night home game against Seton Hall. The tip will be at 8 p.m CT and will be shown on the SEC Network. Roll Tide

item.title: No revisiting 'Sandpapergate': Cricket Australia CEO refuses to re-open investigation over Usman Khawaja's statement
item.description: No revisiting 'Sandpapergate': Cricket Australia CEO refuses to re-open investigation over Usman Khawaja's statement originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Cricket Australia ’s chief executive has made his position clear on Sandpapergate. Usman Khawaja's book revelations have reopened an old and bitter debate. Former teammates are divided, and the board sees little reason to look again. MORE: '100% accurate': David Warner backs Usman Khawaja's Sandpapergate claims, questions Cricket Australia's 2018 investigation CA refuses to budge: Why Cricket Australia won't revisit Sandpapergate despite Usman Khawaja's bombshell Cricket Australia has no plans to go back to ‘Sandpapergate’, and chief executive Todd Greenberg has firmly refused to reopen the investigation despite the startling claims made by Usman Khawaja. The board, he says, is content with how the inquiry into the 2018 ball-tampering affair ended, even though Khawaja now insists that the whole team knew sandpaper was being used on that tour of South Africa. Greenberg's statement arrived just after David Warner threw his weight behind his old teammate, describing the account as “100 per cent accurate” and calling the original investigation “rushed and botched”. MORE: Khawaja sides with Warner, Smith and Bancroft in 'Sandpaper scandal' Khawaja tells his side of the story in his autobiography, Sabr, and it appears to clash with a joint statement released in 2021 by Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon. In that statement, the four bowlers said they had no idea the ball was being tampered with. The left-hander has also spoken of his surprise that Cricket Australia never interviewed him, even though he sat beside Cameron Bancroft throughout the Cape Town Test. Greenberg, however, has made it clear that the book alone will not change the board’s mind. He spoke to SEN about the matter, and his comments touched on his respect for Khawaja, his unwillingness to react to headlines and his belief that nothing useful would come from another inquiry. MORE: ‘We knew': Khawaja blows apart Cummins, Starc's claims of innocence in sandpaper scandal Getty Images Todd Greenberg’s first reaction to Khawaja’s claims about Sandpapergate Greenberg admitted that he had not yet found the time to read the book and said Khawaja had been thoughtful enough to warn him about the release some months earlier. “I haven’t read the book yet. He then spoke about the respect he holds for the batter and explained that he had learned about the claims in the same way as everyone else. “First and foremost, I have huge respect for Usman to give his version of events,” he added. “I read his comments over the weekend in the media, exactly the same time as the public and I’ll obviously get to read his book at some point." MORE: 'He is accurate': Former Aussie quick, part of Sandpapergate tour, backs up Khawaja Next came a note of caution. Greenberg pointed out that parts of Khawaja’s account run against what other people have said, and he stressed that he wants to respond only to the batter’s actual words rather than to the noise around them. He added: “But there are specific details in his book that contradict the versions that have been provided by others. And I want to be really careful to consider what Usman’s actually said, and not respond to the headlines or the subsequent commentary that gets created. “It’s important to attribute his words and not the headlines. It’s important to know that back at that time, players were urged to come forward, and they had the opportunity to do so over these past eight years, and that remains the case.” MORE: Khawaja sides with Warner, Smith and Bancroft in 'Sandpaper scandal' Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft bans: Why Cricket Australia stands by its original investigation The inquiry that followed the Cape Town Test led to 12-month suspensions for Steve Smith and Warner, who were captain and vice-captain at the time. Bancroft, the young opener who handled the sandpaper, was banned for nine months. Greenberg said nothing in Khawaja’s account has shifted the board’s thinking about that process in any way. “We have said we’re comfortable with the outcome of the investigation based on the information we’ve received. That includes what we’ve seen from Usman, and our position hasn’t changed on that,” he said. He went on to rule out a fresh review in plain terms, adding that he cannot see anyone gaining from it. “We don’t see any compelling reason to open the investigation or revisit this again. I don’t think there’s anything that can be gained from that.” Warner has asked for those who ran the original investigation to be held answerable, but Greenberg wondered aloud what a second look would actually achieve. His main worry is that the argument would simply return to where it already stands, with one person’s memory set against another’s. “You end up at the same intersection where one person’s version of events contradicts the others, and I’m not sure what outcome people are searching for,” he said. “I think what people want is a single outcome that everyone is aligned up on, but I don’t think that’s possible on this occasion because we have such conflicting views from the same moment in time.” MORE: 'They cheated': Fans react to Khawaja's Sandpapergate revelations (Getty Images) Why Cricket Australia’s refusal to reopen the Sandpapergate inquiry will not end the debate Greenberg’s argument has a certain logic, since a fresh inquiry could well end up in the same stalemate of clashing memories. However, that is a weak reason to close the door on a matter where Khawaja, the one who sat beside Bancroft throughout the Cape Town Test, was never even asked for his version. The board is also leaning heavily on the idea that players had eight years to come forward. That sounds fair on paper, yet it ignores the fear that many of them must have felt after watching three colleagues serve lengthy bans. It is hard to expect honesty from people who believe that speaking up could cost them their careers. There is a further problem of trust. Warner, Khawaja and the four bowlers are all telling different stories, and the public can see that. A board that simply declares itself comfortable with the outcome will struggle to convince fans that the original process was thorough, especially when it admits that it did not speak to a man who was closest to Bancroft in Cape Town. Cricket Australia need not rewrite the punishments to restore some confidence. A limited, transparent review of how the first investigation was run, and why certain players were never questioned, would cost very little. By refusing even that, the board risks keeping Sandpapergate alive for years to come. For all the latest cricket news, opinion, and commentary, and to share your voice, head to our Facebook , Instagram, and X (Twitter) pages.
