item.content:encoded: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 08: Puka Nacua #12 of the Los Angeles Rams runs the ball against the Washington Commanders during the fourth quarter at Northwest Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) Getty Images We’re about one month out from the start of the fantasy football playoffs. If your roster isn’t being held together by duct tape right now, you’re in great shape. The 2026 NFL season has been brutal from an injury standpoint, and Week 9 brought another onslaught of notable ailments. A handful of starting quarterbacks suffered injuries that could jeopardize their availability for Week 10 and beyond. A pair of starting running backs went down with injuries that will sideline them for at least one week. And a number of fantasy-relevant wide receivers are also on the mend after suffering injuries on Sunday. Every week, we’ll be breaking down the biggest injury news that could shape your fantasy football lineup moving forward. Let’s dive into all of the most notable updates ahead of Week 10. Notable QB Injuries Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes (elbow) The Kansas City Chiefs’ season nearly went off the rails Sunday. Late in the second quarter of their eventual blowout win over the New York Jets, Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes left the field holding his elbow after getting hit by Jets edge-rusher David Bailey as he was attempting a throw. Luckily, he was able to return to the game on the Chiefs’ next offensive possession. Mahomes underwent an MRI after the game, and sources told NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport that the tests “did not reveal a major injury.” Rapoport added that “Mahomes’ elbow strain/sprain will be monitored over the next few days for pain and swell. But so far, so good.” For now, it seems as though Mahomes should be able to suit up in Week 10 against the Atlanta Falcons. But pay close attention to the Chiefs’ injury reports at practice, as it wouldn’t be surprising if Mahomes is limited, especially early in the week. Chargers QB Justin Herbert (hand) Just when you thought the Los Angeles Chargers’ season couldn’t be going any worse, quarterback Justin Herbert left midway through the fourth quarter of his team’s blowout loss to the Houston Texans with an injury to the middle finger on his left (non-throwing) hand. According to ESPN , Herbert “said he wanted to stay in the game, but coach Jim Harbaugh said he overruled him.” However, Harbaugh told reporters Monday that X-rays on Herbert’s hand came back negative for a fracture, “so he should be good to go.” Even with Herbert active, there might not be a single Chargers skill-position player who should be in fantasy lineups in 10- or 12-team leagues. They’ve been that much of a mess this season. Giants QB J.J. McCarthy (hip) New York Giants quarterback left his team’s game against the Philadelphia Eagles in the third quarter with a hip injury after taking a big hit from Eagles linebacker Zack Baun. He missed the Giants’ ensuing drive—and backup Jameis Winston went 6-of-8 for 71 yards and a touchdown on said drive—before returning to finish out the game, albeit hobbled. After the game, McCarthy told reporters that he felt “good” and that “we’re going to do our best to make sure we turn over as fast as possible and do whatever we can between now and then and make sure we’re as close to 100% leading up to a great opponent against Washington.” Unfortunately for McCarthy, the Giants are facing the Commanders on Thursday Night Football in Week 10, so he’s facing a tighter-than-usual turnaround. On Monday, Giants head coach John Harbaugh told reporters that McCarthy is “doing well” and it “does look like he’s going to play” against Washington. But regardless of whether McCarthy or Winston starts under center, Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely should be in all fantasy lineups. Seahawks QB Drew Lock (oblique) Seattle Seahawks starting quarterback Sam Darnold missed his team’s Week 9 win over the Arizona Cardinals with a quad injury and a cracked rib, and he’s not expected to return their Week 10 game against the Las Vegas Raiders, either. But he isn’t the only Seahawks quarterback who’s nursing multiple injuries. Drew Lock, who started in Darnold’s place on Sunday, came into the game with an elbow injury and suffered an oblique injury during the game as well. But during a radio appearance Monday, MacDonald said the Seahawks got a “good exam for Drew” and “I think it’s something we can manage,” according to Seahawks reporter John Boyle . Lock’s availability for Week 10 is great news for fantasy managers who’ve been relying on star wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba. The Seahawks otherwise would have been down to third-string quarterback Jalen Milroe, who has attempted only three regular-season passes thus far in his NFL career. Cardinals QB Gardner Minshew (elbow) On Friday, the Arizona Cardinals officially traded quarterback Jacoby Brissett, whom they benched for Gardner Minshew in Week 8, to the Baltimore Ravens. Three days later, they might be having some seller’s remorse. According to Rapoport , Minshew “is feared to have suffered a torn UCL in his throwing arm” against the Seahawks. He suffered the injury before halftime and played through it in the second half, but Rapoport added that he now might be out for the rest of the season. If that’s the case, rookie quarterback Carson Beck will now be in line to start, albeit with a depleted pass-catching corps. (More on that later.) Beck will have little choice but to pepper tight end Trey McBride with targets moving forward, although McBride’s chances of racking up touchdowns might go down exponentially if Minshew is done for the year. Notable RB Injuries Packers RB Josh Jacobs (finger) Josh Jacobs’ return to the Green Bay Packers lineup didn’t last long. In only his third game back after a six-game suspension, Jacobs suffered a fractured finger in the first quarter of his team’s blowout win over the New England Patriots and did not return. After the game, head coach Matt LaFleur told reporters that “hopefully we can do something to allow him to go out there, but he was just having a hard time gripping the ball.” However, CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reported Monday that Jacobs is “set to undergo surgery on his injured finger this week and is expected to miss a maximum of three weeks.” With Jacobs sidelined, Kaleb Johnson led the way in Green Bay’s backfield with 14 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown, while Pierre Strong Jr. added eight carries for 22 yards. If Marshawn Lloyd returns this week—he missed Sunday’s game with a knee injury—the Packers could be right back to a three-headed backfield that is a fantasy football quagmire. Patriots RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) With fellow New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson dealing with an “ unexpected and unusual medical emergency ,” Rhamondre Stevenson dominated the Patriots’ backfield in Week 8 with a season-high 19 carries for 82 yards. He was on pace for another hefty workload against the Packers—he had six carries for 32 yards and three catches for 46 yards—until he suffered a knee injury in the third quarter and did not return. On Monday, Schefter reported that Stevenson “is dealing with a knee tendon issue that is not expected to require surgery but could sideline him for a short period of time.” Rapoport added that “the injury is to the back of Stevenson’s knee and is expected to keep him out the next few weeks.” Corey Kiner led the Patriots with eight carries for 55 yards and a touchdown against the Packers, so he figures to get the first crack at the starting job with Stevenson and Henderson sidelined. The Pats could always pursue an upgrade on the trade market ahead of the NFL trade deadline at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, too. Notable WR/TE Injuries Rams WR Puka Nacua (knee) With Davante Adams sidelined for the past few weeks, Puka Nacua has become the clear focal point of the Los Angeles

Jacksonville is running away with the AFC South, so it's just now a matter of whether it can lock down the No. 1 seed. 7. Minnesota Vikings 5-2 (5) The Vikings went into Monday night's loss to the Bills averaging only 20 points per game, scoring at a pace with some of the league's worst teams. Carson Wentz failed to give them a spark with struggling Kyler Murray out. They can't win the high-scoring NFC North if they can't find more offense soon. 8. Pittsburgh Steelers 6-2 (8) The Steelers are more confident they can win big in Aaron Rodgers' presumed final season. He's on pace to hit 27 touchdown passes for the 12th time in his career, but he would like to increase his career-low 6.5 yards per passing attempt. MORE: NFL trade deadline predictions for Jonathan Taylor, Daniel Jones and more 9. Seattle Seahawks 5-4 (9) The Seahawks got back to their ideal 50-50 offense to dominate the Cardinals, with 28 Drew Lock passes to match the number of non-Lock runs. The result was 120 rushing yards, finding the right groove with Zach Charbonnet and rookie Jadarian Price, with the latter becoming a receiving factor. 10. Detroit Lions 6-2 (11) The Lions' once-maligned defense has allowed only a total of 62 points during their four-game winning streak. They will get a good test against the Patriots in Munich, Germany, in Week 10, where Jared Goff needs to shake off back-to-back sub 200-yard, one-INT games. 11. Cincinnati Bengals 6-2 (12) Joe Burrow, after picking apart the Falcons downfield in Spain, is up to a league-leading 74.0 completion percentage while still averaging a robust 8.0 yards per attempt. He's on pace for 5,070 passing yards and 49 TDs, which would be one of the all-time great passing seasons. MORE: Joe Burrow, Jordan Love among four QBs who boosted MVP chances Matt Pendleton/Imagn Images via Reuters Connect 12. Green Bay Packers 6-3 (14) The Packers have proved once again Matt LaFleur is locked into their offensive strengths in a given season. He's starting to press and force the issue in the passing game as the defense keeps struggling, not a good formula. 15. So much for knocking him for the Ravens' blown leads. 16. Cleveland Browns 5-4 (16) The Browns' aggressive nature with first-year coach Todd Monken should be applauded. Making the playoffs is less important than finding out whether Sanders can be their franchise QB. MORE: Five reasons why Browns should keep starting Sanders at QB 17. Dallas Cowboys 4-5 (23) The Cowboys are a roller coaster with Brian Schottenheimer and their lack of reliable defense never makes a lead safe, especially when they get too enamored with Dak Prescott's passing. They outlasted the Colts with near-perfect balance, with 37 Prescott dropbacks matched by 34 total runs. That's the formula the Cowboys need: A lot more Javonte Williams. MORE: Ranking 7 trade deadline landing spots for Jonathan Taylor 18. Houston Texans 3-5 (26) C.J. Stroud lit up the Chargers for 384 yards and 5 TDs, bringing him up to an average of 281 yards per game and on pace for 34 TDs. He's averaging 8.0 yards per attempt with a 112.1 passer rating. He's all but locked up his lucrative second contract. 19. Las Vegas Raiders 4-5 (18) The Raiders went to San Francisco, allowing an average of 146.4 rushing yards per game, the second-highest total in the NFL. They gave up 190 to a 49ers combination led by McCaffrey and rookie Kaelon Black. They also only ran for 24. That kind of disparity doesn't add up to winning games. 20. Baltimore Ravens 4-5 (17) The Ravens might be trying to move Derrick Henry, but they can't expect to be competitive without a mobile quarterback and with a shaky offensive li

item.title: The Bills are in first place in the AFC following their Monday night win
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 09: Terrel Bernard #8 of the Buffalo Bills celebrates with teammates after intercepting a pass intended for Justin Jefferson #18 of the Minnesota Vikings during the third quarter of the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 09, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills beat the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night to hold onto their spot atop the AFC. It wasn’t easy, but the Bills put enough points on the board to get it done. In the AFC East, the New England Patriots also lost as did the New York Jets and Miami Dolphins. The Bills are up two games in the win column and three games in the loss column. A dominating lead in the division right now with plenty of games left. The AFC divisional leaders aw the Jacksonville Jaguars win on Thursday nigh tand the Denver Broncos win on Sunday with the Pittsburgh Steelers on a bye. The seven AFC playoff teams seem pretty darn set. AFC playoff standings after Bills’ MNF win 1. Buffalo Bills (7-1) 2. Denver Broncos (7-2) 3. Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2, 5-2 AFC) 4. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2, win over CIN, 3-2 AFC) 5. Kansas City Chiefs (6-2, 6-1 AFC) 6. Cincinnati Bengals (6-2, loss to PIT, 4-2 AFC) 7. New England Patriots (5-4, 5-1 AFC) 8. Cleveland Browns (5-4, 3-3 AFC) 9. Las Vegas Raiders (4-5, 3-3 AFC) 10. Baltimore Ravens (4-5, 2-4 AFC) 11. Houston Texans (3-5) 12. New York Jets (2-7, 2-4 AFC) 13. Indianapolis Colts (2-7, 1-5 AFC) 14. Miami Dolphins (1-7, 1-4 AFC) 15. Tennessee Titans (1-7, 1-5 AFC) 16. Los Angeles Chargers (0-8) Explaining the 6-2 logjam in the AFC playoff standings The Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals are both 6-2, so they first have to settle the AFC North leader. Pittsburgh’s win over the Bengals slots the Steelers into the division lead. Among the division leaders, the Jaguars and Steelers haven’t played each other so the Jags’ 5-2 AFC record slots them third in front of the Steelers. In the Wild card, the Chiefs and Bengals are tied. The Chiefs have the best AFC record at 6-1, so they fill in at fifth. The Bengals are sixth.

item.title: Oregon braces for a 'different' Michigan after OC firing, QB shake-up
item.description: The Oregon football team and coach Dan Lanning are set to take on a reeling Michigan program with a fired offensive coordinator and major questions at quarterback. Sound familiar? The Ducks (6-3, 4-2 Big Ten) went through their own offensive crisis in mid-October, fired offensive play-caller Drew Mehringer and shuffled quarterbacks before finally hitting their groove in each of the last two weeks. Lanning is expecting the Wolverines (5-4, 2-4) to look like a different team this Saturday, Nov. 14, at Autzen Stadium. "Teams that have done that and experienced that recently, they’ve kind of had a resurgence on offense," Lanning said during his Nov. 9 press conference. And Lanning isn't just talking about his Ducks . The fifth-year coach has shown his players clips, stats and other information around programs that have made major coaching changes midseason and performed significantly better in the ensuing weeks. "We’ve seen a lot of those teams have a lot of success," Lanning said. "And sometimes that’s not just because of a change, but there’s a spark that’s sometimes lit when those things happen. We anticipate to see their absolute best and we’re going to have to chase ghosts a little bit and look for every answer that we might be able to find based on what might be different." Michigan has been putrid offensively over the last month-plus, ranking nearly dead-last in college football in total offense (302.6 yards per game) and scoring offense (19.6 points per game). The Wolverines are fresh off a miserable offensive showing in a rivalry loss to Michigan State last weekend at home, scoring a meager six points and turning the ball over four times. Bryce Underwood, a former consensus five-star recruit, was benched at quarterback for freshman Tommy Carr, but neither signal caller has had much success this season. Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham, who is in his first season in Ann Arbor after 22 seasons as the head coach of Utah, said he'd re-evaluate the QB situation this weekend. He also fired his OC, Jason Beck. Underwood has completed 58.1% of his passes for 924 yards, five touchdowns and six interceptions while Carr has completed 67% of his throws for 641 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions. "More recently, I think if you look at it, it’s about who’s been protecting the ball better," Lanning said of the Michigan QBs. "Bryce, obviously, the strength of his arm and as a running threat is unique. But they both operate some similar – it isn’t like the offense completely changes based on which guy’s in the game. There’s still some similarities in what they do." item.content:encoded: The Oregon football team and coach Dan Lanning are set to take on a reeling Michigan program with a fired offensive coordinator and major questions at quarterback. Sound familiar? The Ducks (6-3, 4-2 Big Ten) went through their own offensive crisis in mid-October, fired offensive play-caller Drew Mehringer and shuffled quarterbacks before finally hitting their groove in each of the last two weeks. Lanning is expecting the Wolverines (5-4, 2-4) to look like a different team this Saturday, Nov. 14, at Autzen Stadium. "Teams that have done that and experienced that recently, they’ve kind of had a resurgence on offense," Lanning said during his Nov. 9 press conference. And Lanning isn't just talking about his Ducks . The fifth-year coach has shown his players clips, stats and other information around programs that have made major coaching changes midseason and performed significantly better in the ensuing weeks. "We’ve seen a lot of those teams have a lot of success," Lanning said. "And sometimes that’s not just because of a change, but there’s a spark that’s sometimes lit when those things happen. We anticipate to see their absolute best and we’re going to have to chase ghosts a little bit and look for every answer that we might be able to find based on what might be different." Michigan has been putrid offensively over the last month-plus, ranking nearly dead-last in college football in total offense (302.6 yards per game) and scoring offense (19.6 points per game). The Wolverines are fresh off a miserable offensive showing in a rivalry loss to Michigan State last weekend at home, scoring a meager six points and turning the ball over four times. Bryce Underwood, a former consensus five-star recruit, was benched at quarterback for freshman Tommy Carr, but neither signal caller has had much success this season. Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham, who is in his first season in Ann Arbor after 22 seasons as the head coach of Utah, said he'd re-evaluate the QB situation this weekend. He also fired his OC, Jason Beck. Underwood has completed 58.1% of his passes for 924 yards, five touchdowns and six interceptions while Carr has completed 67% of his throws for 641 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions. "More recently, I think if you look at it, it’s about who’s been protecting the ball better," Lanning said of the Michigan QBs. "Bryce, obviously, the strength of his arm and as a running threat is unique. But they both operate some similar – it isn’t like the offense completely changes based on which guy’s in the game. There’s still some similarities in what they do." Lanning said the Ducks will look back at film of Michigan's newest play-caller, offensive line coach Jim Harding, and do a deep dive of what Whittingham's offenses have looked like over the years in Salt Lake City. "I know (Whittingham's) a Hall of Fame coach for a reason and he’s won a lot of football games," Lanning said. "I’ve been worrying about my own problems and not really paying attention to his, but I know he does a great job. I’m sure they’ll be prepared to play us." Alec Dietz covers University of Oregon football and women’s basketball for The Register-Guard. You may reach him at adietz@registerguard.com . Want to see more Oregon Ducks coverage? Subscribe to The Register-Guard’s newsletter . This article originally appeared on Register-Guard: Oregon braces for a 'different' Michigan after OC firing, QB shake-up

After four seasons at UC Santa Barbara, Gabe Vincent entered the 2018 NBA draft. He went undrafted but was signed to an Exhibit 10 contract by the Sacramento Kings. He played the first two seasons of his pro basketball career in the NBA G League with the Kings’ affiliate team, the Stockton Kings. The Miami Heat signed him to a two-way contract midway through the 2019-20 NBA season. He had his breakout campaign during the 2022-23 season, when the Heat made it all the way to the NBA Finals against the Denver Nuggets . Vincent averaged 9.4 points, 2.1 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game in the regular season. He was even better during their NBA Finals run, putting up 12.7 points, 1.4 rebounds and 3.5 assists in 22 games as the Heat lost to the Nuggets in five. The Los Angeles Lakers signed him that summer to a three-year, $33 million contract. However, his debut season with the Lakers was marred by a knee injury, limiting him to just 11 games. He never got his footing in Los Angeles and was traded to the Atlanta Hawks midway through the final year of his deal. item.title: Vikings trade rumor details deadline plans at quarterback, two potential options
item.description: Nobody was expecting Minnesota Vikings quarterback Carson Wentz to play at an elite level on Monday night, but I’m not sure anyone expected him to play that bad. Saying Wentz struggled against the Buffalo Bills would be an understatement. The veteran signal-caller had one of the worst performances anyone has ever seen from a quarterback. And, that performance, along with the struggles Kyler Murray has seen this season, leaves the Vikings with a desperate need for a quarterback trade. On that front, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that the Vikings will explore a trade for a quarterback at the deadline, which falls on Tuesday, Nov. 10, at 4 p.m. ET. MORE: Puka Nacua injury update from Rams confirms severity, return timeline “I know the Minnesota Vikings are going to explore their options (at quarterback),” Rapoport said during the Monday Night Football broadcast. Rapoport went on to mention both Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins and Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones as potential options. However, Rapoport notes that the Raiders have shown zero interest in wanting to trade Cousins. MORE: Josh Jacobs injury update confirms need for surgery, return timeline “They actually have two pretty good options… Here’s what the Vikings have: they have Kirk Cousins, obviously played for them, played for Kevin O’Connell. The Raiders have shown no indication that they would trade him, but at least they could call and see what is there. “And then they have Daniel Jones, who obviously was in their building a couple of years ago on the practice squad. Playing still for the Colts. A Colts season that has gone the opposite of where they want to go. Those are two pretty solid options who could be had for draft pick compensation that wouldn’t kill the Vikings. I would expect them to at least look into it tomorrow.” Are Kirk Cousins, Daniel Jones available? Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins (8) signals during the second quarter against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi’s Stadium. Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) As Rapoport noted, the Raiders appear to be keen on keeping Cousins and it’s understandable why, as Las Vegas still has a shot at the playoffs. Jones is probably the more realistic option because of the impending fire sale the Colts appear set to embark on. But The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reported over the weekend that the Colts informed Jones they will not trade him at the deadline. MORE: Troy Aikman, Joe Buck able to laugh again thanks to Wentz’ performance “The Colts informed QB Daniel Jones on Saturday they’re not trading him by Tuesday’s deadline,” Pelissero wrote. Now, as we’ve seen in recent weeks, just about anyone can be had if a team is willing to overpay. It’s conceivable the Vikings could do just that to land either Cousins or Jones. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: 3 Key Takeaways from Hornets Big Win Over Cavaliers
item.description: Cleveland Cavaliers guard Tyrese Proctor (24) shoots the ball defended by Charlotte Hornets forward Tidjane Salaun (31) during the game at Spectrum Center | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Daniel Benjamin, Editor The Charlotte Hornets snapped a six-game losing skid with an emphatic 124-112 victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers at Spectrum Center on Monday night. Operating without key rotational pillars Brandon Miller, Kon Knueppel, Dennis Schröder , Moussa Diabaté , and Grant Williams , head coach Charles Lee’s starting group generated unexpected answers against a formidable Eastern Conference opponent. Rather than folding under structural strain, Charlotte controlled the game’s rhythm from deep, pushing their lead to as many as 33 points before navigating late-game turbulence. Beyond the surprising final score, three critical post-game takeaways stand out from Charlotte’s performance. Grayson Allen and Naz Reid Deliver Primary Offensive Punch Charlotte Hornets guard Grayson Allen (8) makes a slam dunk against the Cleveland Cavaliers during the game at Spectrum Center. Photo Credit: Jim Dedmon, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect With the Hornets number-one option, Miller, sidelined , Charlotte required high usage from its established veterans. Grayson Allen and Naz Reid stepped into the spotlight and completely anchored the offense. Allen put on an absolute perimeter shooting display, pouring in a team-high 27 points while knocking down 6-of-12 three-pointers. His sharp movement off screens and willingness to pull up in transition kept Cleveland’s defense stretched out and unable to pack the paint. Operating alongside him in the frontcourt, Reid put together a dominant 25-point, 13-rebound double-double. He punished Cleveland out of the high post, knocking down four triples of his own while grabbing 12 defensive boards to secure possessions. Combined, Allen and Reid supplied 52 points, giving Charlotte the exact scoring firepower required to dictate terms. Ryan Kalkbrenner’s Glass Control Changes the Game Charlotte Hornets center Ryan Kalkbrenner (11) back on defense against Cleveland Cavaliers forward Riley Minix (12) during the first half at Spectrum Center. Photo Credit: Jim Dedmon, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect While Allen and Reid provided the headline scoring stats, Ryan Kalkbrenner delivered the most impactful interior performance of the night. Facing a physical Cleveland frontcourt, Kalkbrenner fundamentally altered the game’s physical dynamic through relentless work on the boards. Kalkbrenner snatched a game-high 15 total rebounds, highlighted by a staggering 10 offensive rebounds. His relentless effort on the glass repeatedly extended Charlotte possessions, leading to vital second-chance points that systematically broke Cleveland’s defensive momentum. Grayson Allen and Naz Reid Deliver Primary Offensive Punch Charlotte Hornets guard Grayson Allen (8) makes a slam dunk against the Cleveland Cavaliers during the game at Spectrum Center. Photo Credit: Jim Dedmon, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect With the Hornets number-one option, Miller, sidelined , Charlotte required high usage from its established veterans. Ryan Kalkbrenner’s Glass Control Changes the Game Charlotte Hornets center Ryan Kalkbrenner (11) back on defense against Cleveland Cavaliers forward Riley Minix (12) during the first half at Spectrum Center. Photo Credit: Jim Dedmon, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect While Allen and Reid provided the headline scoring stats, Ryan Kalkbrenner delivered the most impactful interior performance of the night. Facing a physical Cleveland frontcourt, Kalkbrenner fundamentally altered the game’s physical dynamic through relentless work on the boards. Kalkbrenner snatched a game-high 15 total rebounds, highlighted by a staggering 10 offensive rebounds. His relentless effort on the glass repeatedly extended Charlotte possessions, leading to vital second-chance points that systematically broke Cleveland’s defensive momentum. Anchoring the defense with three blocked shots and finishing as a team-best plus-20 on the night, Kalkbrenner gave Lee elite rim protection and interior muscle that offset Cleveland’s baseline height advantage. Balanced Perimeter Spacing Offsets Backcourt Constraints With Coby White operating on a managed 20-minute workload, Charlotte’s backcourt structure required disciplined execution from secondary contributors. White managed the floor effectively, finishing with 9 assists against just 3 turnovers, while Charlotte’s secondary floor-spacers kept the offense flowing during bench shifts. Tidjane Salaün provided crucial scoring relief during his shift, knocking down three triples en route to 14 points. Meanwhile, Christian Anderson Jr. added 9 points on 3-of-4 shooting from deep off the bench, and Sion James chipped in 11 points. As a collective unit, the Hornets connected on 23-of-46 three-point attempts (50%), weaponizing pristine floor spacing to reverse their recent shooting struggles. Last Word on Hornets Big Win This victory over Cleveland is far more important than just a single home win; it provides a clear operational blueprint for Lee’s system moving forward. Navigating severe injury hits forces young players like Kalkbrenner, Salaün Anderson Jr. and Steinbach into high-leverage roles where developmental growth accelerates out of necessity. While health remains the primary factor for Charlotte’s ultimate ceiling this season, executing a 124-point performance while curbing live-ball turnovers proves that Lee’s culture and tactical principles can win games even under heavy structural strain. item.title: Lakers big Walker Kessler’s take on Collin Sexton team-up will hit Jazz fans in the feels
item.description: Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Lakers big Walker Kessler’s take on Collin Sexton team-up will hit Jazz fans in the feels appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With the Los Angeles Lakers being on the second night of a back-to-back, they decided to sit out Austin Reaves — with Luka Doncic coming back from a one-game absence. This left a secondary playmaking void for the Lakers, which Collin Sexton gladly filled. He finished with 18 points and six assists in a 124-114 win over the Atlanta Hawks, and his chemistry with Walker Kessler was also in full display. Sexton and Kessler have pre-existing chemistry dating back to their time together on the Utah Jazz. They played together for three full seasons, so it’s not too surprising that the Lakers are benefitting from the connection these two have. Kessler also had a big game against the Hawks, thanks in part to some dimes he got from Sexton, finishing with 21 points, 10 rebounds, four assists, one steal, and one block. “That goes back a long time ago. I’ve known him for a long time, so we definitely got really good chemistry,” Kessler said after the game, per Benjamin Royer of the Orange County Register. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Lakers would have had a much more difficult time on the night if it weren’t for Sexton . He caused havoc on both ends against the Hawks, and it’s his relentlessness when going downhill that opened up a lot of scoring opportunities for his former Jazz teammate. Kessler on the other hand, continues to be a monster on both ends of the floor — proving to be well worth the $130 million the Lakers committed to him in a sign-and-trade this offseason. He plays absolutely huge, contests nearly every shot, and he provides solidity on the glass as well. The Lakers are now 10-2 on the season, and their offseason dealings have looked like genius moves thus far. They have the league’s best offense, with Doncic leading the way and his supporting cast doing its job, and they will look to keep it going on Wednesday against the Milwaukee Bucks. Related: Lakers star Luka Doncic’s 73-point outburst gets eye-opening comment from Quin Snyder Related: Skip Bayless takes not-so-subtle dig at LeBron James while celebrating Lakers’ early success

item.title: Horsepower or Horseplay? Individual performances to highlight from Colts’ Week 9 loss to Cowboys
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 8: Seth McGowan #20 of the Indianapolis Colts celebrates during the fourth quarter of a game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 8, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts lost to the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, 23-27, which wasn’t unexpected by any means given that the season has quickly snowballed into another lost year—with a fire sale now fully underway. To their credit, the reeling Colts, who have now lost 5 straight games and 14 of their last 16 games dating back to last season’s brutal final stretch, showed more fight than in last weekend’s blowout ‘laugher’ loss in Jacksonville. Let’s get to the positives, the negatives, and maybe even a little in between: Horsepower Young Defensive Line: Despite veteran DeForest Buckner having departed back to the Bay, it was impressive to watch some of the ‘young pup’ Colts defensive linemen battle out there, including defensive tackle Ade Adebawore (5 QB pressures) , rookie Caden Curry (a sack and a fumble recovery), Laiatu Latu (a sack), and yes, even 2nd-year pro Jaylahn Tuimoloau (a sack), who’s begun to finally round into form, with longtime nose tackle Grover Stewart remaining the ‘veteran voice.’ RB Seth McGowan: In the midst of Jonathan Taylor trade rumors, McGowan has seen an increased workload as of late and taken advantage, averaging 7.5 yards per carry on 6 carries in this one, including a short 2-yard touchdown run near midway through the first quarter . I still think I’d ideally like McGowan more as a change-of-pace or the 2nd head of a two headed running back attack, than a featured every down rusher, but the rookie 7th round pick has been a pleasant find for Indianapolis so far this season and could be poised for a bigger role if Taylor is indeed moved before Tuesday’s trade deadline. WR Ashton Dulin: The 29-year-old continues to be one of the longer tenured ‘fan favorites’ still remaining on the Colts roster, as he’s gone from undrafted free agent to core special teamer to even starting wideout at times. Dulin showcased his elite speed in this one, turning a short Colts quarterback Daniel Jones wide receiver screen pass into a 55-yard touchdown catch-and-run down the sideline . Rookie Defenders: Safety Hunter Wohler, who missed all of his debut season with a season-ending Lisfranc injury, had a team-high 16 tackles (6 solo) filling in for injured starting rookie safety AJ Haulcy and was a force in run defense. Meanwhile, the pair of Colts rookie linebackers were also active, as CJ Allen had 10 tackles (4 solo) and Bryce Boettcher added 12 tackles (4 solo) respectively. That’ll certainly play. Spencer Shrader: Having his worst game of the season 2 weeks ago in Minnesota, Shrader looked more like himself, converting all 3 of his field goal attempts of 47-yards, 59-yards, and 50-yards . Perhaps most telling, the Cowboys coaching staff changed their minds on accepti

Let’s get to the positives, the negatives, and maybe even a little in between: Horsepower Young Defensive Line: Despite veteran DeForest Buckner having departed back to the Bay, it was impressive to watch some of the ‘young pup’ Colts defensive linemen battle out there, including defensive tackle Ade Adebawore (5 QB pressures) , rookie Caden Curry (a sack and a fumble recovery), Laiatu Latu (a sack), and yes, even 2nd-year pro Jaylahn Tuimoloau (a sack), who’s begun to finally round into form, with longtime nose tackle Grover Stewart remaining the ‘veteran voice.’ RB Seth McGowan: In the midst of Jonathan Taylor trade rumors, McGowan has seen an increased workload as of late and taken advantage, averaging 7.5 yards per carry on 6 carries in this one, including a short 2-yard touchdown run near midway through the first quarter . I still think I’d ideally like McGowan more as a change-of-pace or the 2nd head of a two headed running back attack, than a featured every down rusher, but the rookie 7th round pick has been a pleasant find for Indianapolis so far this season and could be poised for a bigger role if Taylor is indeed moved before Tuesday’s trade deadline. WR Ashton Dulin: The 29-year-old continues to be one of the longer tenured ‘fan favorites’ still remaining on the Colts roster, as he’s gone from undrafted free agent to core special teamer to even starting wideout at times. Dulin showcased his elite speed in this one, turning a short Colts quarterback Daniel Jones wide receiver screen pass into a 55-yard touchdown catch-and-run down the sideline . Rookie Defenders: Safety Hunter Wohler, who missed all of his debut season with a season-ending Lisfranc injury, had a team-high 16 tackles (6 solo) filling in for injured starting rookie safety AJ Haulcy and was a force in run defense. Meanwhile, the pair of Colts rookie linebackers were also active, as CJ Allen had 10 tackles (4 solo) and Bryce Boettcher added 12 tackles (4 solo) respectively. That’ll certainly play. Spencer Shrader: Having his worst game of the season 2 weeks ago in Minnesota, Shrader looked more like himself, converting all 3 of his field goal attempts of 47-yards, 59-yards, and 50-yards . Perhaps most telling, the Cowboys coaching staff changed their minds on accepting a penalty, which the officiating crew said was legal(?), when they saw Shrader trotting on the field for a potential 61-yard field goal attempt. Horseplay QB Daniel Jones: At one point, the Colts had just 8 total passing yards midway through the 2nd quarter. Look, some of the wideouts playing meaningful snaps are preseason guys, and the offensive line hasn’t been great, especially in light of trading All-Pro left guard Quenton Nelson. However, it’s hard to win when your starting quarterback is dinking and dunking or checking down and rarely challenges the opposing defense downfield. At a certain point, you have to trust your receivers to win their one-on-one matchups downfield. This wasn’t a great Dallas defense coming in either, surrendering the 27th most points (26.6 avg. ppg). Jones’ game-sealing interception facing pass pressure off his back foot was about as predictable as it gets. RB: Jonathan Taylor: The main topic of ongoing national Colts trade rumors hasn’t looked like himself the past two weeks, perhaps making ‘business decisions’ or maybe because with limited carries in back-to-back games, he’s had trouble getting into the flow of the game. I’ve always thought Taylor is someone who gets better during the course of a game with the more carries he gets, sort of like a heavyweight fighter wearing the opponent down round-after-round, before eventually breaking a big ‘TKO’ run late. I’m not going to make excuses for him, because his fumble early in the 4th quarter with the Colts threatening to score a touchdown in the red zone simply can’t happen—and he has to keep his pad level down for that matter. That being said, if Taylor stays past the deadline, I think he’ll look more like his old self. I wouldn’t expect him to get 30 carries in a game anymore this season, but closer to the 20 carry mark we’ve seen. WR Josh Downs: Normally “Mr. Reliable” as a 3rd down slot target, Downs has been “Mr. Drops” over the past two weeks since reportedly requesting a trade from the Colts. He had a 3rd and 8 drop early in the 2nd quarte r , and then followed suit again with 1:45 left in the 4th quarter . If Downs wants to depart, fine, but he hasn’t backed up his surprising request with his play on the field, when such trade requests are typically reserved for more proven players with a longstanding history of production. The Colts are holding out hope for a 3rd round pick to move him, but after his recent performances, they may be realistically still looking at a 4th round pick. In the battle of ‘Downs brothers,’ his younger brother, starting Dallas safety, Caleb Downs, clearly got the upper hand of big brother with the game-clinching interception off Jones, a sack, and even better for him, leaving Indy with the road win. CB Sauce Gardner: Look, Sauce didn’t make the trade for the Colts to acquire him for two first round picks and AD Mitchell, but Indianapolis clearly hasn’t gotten the return for an elite shutdown cornerback that they were envisioning to-date. I actually thought Sauce had played well in this one, until he gave up a back-breaking 46-yard reception to Cowboys wideout Ryan Flournoy with 1:24 left that set up Dallas for the would-be game-winning touchdown. This wasn’t even All-Pro CeeDee Lamb who beat him deep, as an elite wideout that I could actually live with. Gardner’s just given up too many big plays downfield this year.

item.title: Rookie of the Year winners announced, who will get traded & setting the scene for the GM meetings
item.description: Subscribe to Baseball Bar-B-Cast Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube The Rookie of the Year award winners have been announced, with Detroit Tigers infielder Kevin McGonigle winning in the American League and Cincinnati Reds first baseman Sal Stewart winning in the National League, taking home the honors. While both rookies winning wasn’t a complete surprise, there was tight competition in both leagues that had many guessing whether there would be unanimous winners or some split calls. On this episode of the Baseball Bar-B-Cast, Jake Mintz and Jordan Shusterman talk about the award winners, including Jordan discussing his semi-controversial ballot that awarded Cleveland Guardians pitcher Parker Messick one of his two first-place votes and why McGonigle was also deserving of winning the award. They then take a look at the rest of the voting and see if there were any notable vote-getters in what was an extremely strong rookie class. Later in the show, Jake and Jordan each draft five players they think are most likely to be traded this offseason due to the not-as-strong free-agent class we've become accustomed to. They then set the scene live in Las Vegas for the GM meetings, which are set to take place on Tuesday. item.content:encoded: How to watch New Zealand vs. India in the 3rd ODI cricket match, including live stream, TV channel, start time in NZ, India, US and UK. Getty India's Axar Patel plays a shot during the 2nd ODI cricket match between New Zealand and India in Wellington on November 7, 2026. Getty WELLINGTON, NEW ZEALAND - ans show their support during game two of the Men's One Day International series between New Zealand and India at Hnry Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Wellington, New Zealand. Getty India can clinch its ODI series against New Zealand on Monday night, when the third game starts at 9 p.m. ET in Hamilton. A win ends the series with two matches to spare, leaving an injury-hit New Zealand needing a victory to stay alive about a year before the 2027 Cricket World Cup. Outside the United States, the match falls on Tuesday. First ball at Seddon Park, a day-night fixture, comes at 3 p.m. NZDT, which works out to 8 p.m. CT, 7 p.m. MT and 6 p.m. PT on Monday for American viewers. Fans in India wake up to a 7:30 a.m. IST on Tuesday start, with the toss around 7 a.m. In the United Kingdom, play begins at 2 a.m. GMT on Tuesday. HOW TO WATCH: NEW ZEALAND vs. INDIA, 3RD ODI India tour of New Zealand 2026 • Seddon Park, Hamilton • Day-night match • India leads the five-match ODI series 2-0 Region Start Time TV Streaming USA Monday, Nov. 9, 2026 9 p.m. ET 8 p.m. CT 7 p.m. MT 6 p.m. PT Willow TV (cable/satellite) Fubo; Willow app / Willow by Cricbuzz (direct subscription, $10 a month or $80 a year); also platforms that carry Willow. Official site: willow.tv India Tuesday, Nov. 10, 2026 7:30 a.m. IST (toss ~7 a.m. IST) Sony Sports Network (e.g., Sony Ten 1, Sony Ten 3; HD/SD; multiple language feeds including Hindi) SonyLIV app and website (subscription required): sonyliv.com New Zealand Tuesday, Nov. 10, 2026 3 p.m. NZDT Sky Sport NZ Sky Go and Sky Sport Now: skysportnow.co.nz . Sky holds rights for the home internationals. UK Tuesday, Nov. 10, 2026 2 a.m. GMT TNT Sports (TNT Sports 1 for the 3rd ODI; also listed on TNT Sports 2/4 for other matches) discovery+ or packages including TNT Sports/HBO Max: tntsports.co.uk Sources: Sporting News (US) ; Sporting News (India) ; CNET ; News18 ; Business Standard ; CricRadar ; CricketNews ; TechRadar . Where to Watch New Zealand vs. India on TV and Streaming Getty India’s Axar Patel plays a shot during the 2nd ODI cricket match between New Zealand and India in Wellington on November 7, 2026. U.S. viewers can find the match on Willow TV through cable or satellite. Fubo carries the channel for streaming, and fans can subscribe directly through Willow by Cricbuzz for $10 a month or $80 a year. In India, Sony Sports Network televises the series on Sony Ten 1 and Sony Ten 3, in high definition and standard definition, with Hindi among the language feeds. Streaming runs through the SonyLIV app and website , which requires a subscription. In New Zealand, Sky Sport NZ has the broadcast because the network holds the rights to home internationals . Streaming goes through Sky Go and Sky Sport Now . In the United Kingdom, TNT Sports 1 airs the third ODI , while TNT Sports 2 and 4 also show other matches in the series. Streaming is available through discovery+ or any package including TNT Sports . New Zealand vs. India Preview Getty Fans show their support during game two of the Men’s One Day International series between New Zealand and India at Hnry Stadium on Nov. 7, 2026 in Wellington, New Zealand. India leads the five-match series 2-0 after a five-wicket win in Auckland on Nov. 4 and a four-run victory in Wellington on Nov. 7. Rain interrupted both games, so the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method decided each result. A third loss would hand India the best-of-five series with two matches left to play. More wet weather is in the forecast for Hamilton, and the surface favors seam bowling , according to Cricbuzz . That raises the importance of the toss. New Zealand has won its last 12 completed ODIs at Seddon Park. For the home side, it’s win the match or lose the series. The tour sits roughly a year ahead of the 2027 Cricket World Cup, to be hosted in Africa with matches held across South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia. Moisture, seam movement and rain delays have produced attritional, low-scoring cricket in place of the big totals common in the modern white-ball game, which gives both teams World Cup preparation in difficult conditions. Shubman Gill captains India in this match, with Shreyas Iyer due to take over later in the series as Gill prepares for Test cricket. The pace attack is young (Anshul Kamboj, Auqib Nabi, Gurnoor Brar and Arshdeep Singh) and has performed well so far. The batting order leans on Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli at the top, with Iyer and KL Rahul behind them. India is expected to keep its winning combination : Rohit Sharma, Gill (captain), Virat Kohli, Iyer, KL Rahul (wicketkeeper), Naman Dhir, Axar Patel, Kamboj, Nabi, Brar and Arshdeep Singh, in that batting order. Dhir and Patel could swap places, and Mohammed Siraj or Kuldeep Yadav could enter, though the younger pace group has been preferred to date. Injuries dictate New Zealand’s selection. Blair Tickner has been stood down, Matt Henry targets a fourth ODI return and Lockie Ferguson is dealing with a calf issue. That leaves captain Mitchell Santner with this expected batting order, according to Cricinfo : Will Young, Tim Seifert, Henry Nicholls, Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Tom Latham (wicketkeeper), Santner, Nathan Smith, Kyle Jamieson, Matt Fisher or Kristian Clarke, and Jacob Duffy. Final lineups arrive at the toss. A New Zealand victory would cut the deficit to 2-1 and send the series to a fourth game with everything still open. item.title: CF Montreal are for sale: What it means, how much it could cost, and what’s next for the MLS club
item.description: In an emotional press conference, CF Montreal’s founder and owner Joey Saputo refused to rule out relocation In a rare press conference, CF Montreal owner Joey Saputo announced that his family was beginning the process of “initiating a structured sale process” of the MLS club. Saputo informed the public of his intentions on Monday afternoon, pausing multiple times to fight back tears after over three decades of owning the Quebecois club. “This decision is neither driven by urgency, nor dictated by circumstance,” Saputo said in his initial scripted remarks. “It’s the result of a careful and deliberate reflection on where we stand today, and more importantly, on the opportunities that lie ahead for the club.” Continue reading...

item.title: Cerebral Josh King plots unusual route into Tuchel’s England plans
item.description: Armed with an impressive academic record and experience as a rugby fly-half, the teenager is anything but typical Josh King is talking with pride about how his mother, Michelle, a university lecturer, has almost finished her PhD in sickle cell disease. The Fulham attacking midfielder, who is in the England squad for the Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain this week, mentions that his father, Steve, is a lawyer and says he might have liked to follow in his footsteps if it had not worked out for him on the pitch. King’s background is not that of a typical footballer. Privately educated at Hampton School in south-west London, he aced his GCSEs, achieving A or A* in his 10 subjects. He went on to study part-time for A-levels in French, maths and psychology, getting grades of A, C and D – pretty impressive, especially when you consider he sat the exams in a hotel suite in Romania in the summer of last year while playing for England at the European Under-19 Championship. Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester’s soulless content machine football clubs sum up post-imperial Britain | Barney Ronay
item.description: United and City dominate the news cycle with stories so strange and vast they threaten to consume the rest of the league In Manchester this weekend it was possible to bookend your Thursday‑to‑Sunday entertainment with two cultural events. First up, a debut screening of the re‑released and uncensored Ken Russell film The Devils at Trafford Odeon. And three days later, three miles down the road, Manchester United versus Aston Villa at Old Trafford. As expected, one of these events provided a visceral cinematic experience, a deeply disturbing two-hour public meditation on the meaning of faith, blood, fear, power, ritual and the fetishising of objects, climaxing in an orgiastic crowd scene of depraved but undeniably erotic abandon, all acted out on a set in a state of glorious and performative ruin. And the other one was a film with Oliver Reed in it. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Manchester United, Aston Villa and the unseriousness of a 4-4 draw
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Precisely 13,266 games have been played since the inception of the Premier League, and 19 of those matches have finished 4-4 (0.1%), a rarity in a division dominated by the mighty 1-0 (17.6%). It was about time we got one, though. The months of August and September, when teams are still fighting to define their top-flight seasons and fitness and motivation tend to be at their peak, have never seen a single 4-4 draw. As motivation decreases the chances of stupid scorelines increase, and that’s where the 4-4 creeps in. There’s a certain on-the-beachness inherent in the score, and it is no coincidence that it has occurred more in the second half of April, as thoughts drift to the close season and the ineffable pointlessness of a lot of late-campaign football becomes unavoidable, than in the entirety of any other month. Students, teachers and visitors at the University of Queensland can view the world’s longest-running experiment. The flamin’ pitch drop experiment began in 1930 and is designed to demonstrate how an apparent solid (pitch) behaves like an extremely viscous liquid. Nearly 100 years ago pitch was placed in a funnel and kept at room temperature. It moves incredibly slowly at a rate of approximately one atom per second (slower than the continental drift), and only nine drips have ever been recorded , though never witnessed. Without the need for intercontinental travel, perhaps other readers can now appreciate what it’s like to watch Arsenal win 1-0 ” – John Holtom. Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City’s weaknesses under Enzo Maresca are being exposed
item.description: After three straight defeats, City’s manager says he will use the international break to reassess. Their problems may go beyond tactics Sign up for our free newsletter here Enzo Maresca seemed, if not quite baffled by his side’s Saturday defeat to Nottingham Forest, then at least a little put out. After seven straight wins from the start of the season, that’s now three straight defeats, a pattern so unusual that it’s been recorded only once before in top-flight English history, by Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05. The three defeats were all different, Maresca said, although in all of them City had had more possession and more chances. In the 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa two weeks ago, City had 63% of the ball and had 15 chances to Villa’s eight. In the 1-0 home defeat to Brighton last weekend, they had 62% possession and 21 chances to seven. At the City Ground, it was 79% possession and 12 chances to 11. So Maresca is right in one way: City could look at basic statistics and say they had been unfortunate – although Forest could equally point to the fact that they went into that game third top of the expected goals table but second-bottom of the actual table. This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

item.description: Roma and Lazio have both made unbeaten starts to the Serie A season, giving those in the Italian capital dreams of a Scudetto After nine games in 28 days, Gian Piero Gasperini finally got a moment to pause and reflect on Sunday night. The Roma manager was back in Liguria, where he worked for the best part of a decade across two stints at Genoa, to collect an award from Stelle Nello Sport – an association formed to promote sport in the region – celebrating his career achievements and commitment to courageous attacking football. The timing worked out well. Gasperini’s Roma thumped Sassuolo 3-0 on Saturday, bouncing back from a midweek defeat against Manchester United . That result meant the Giallorossi had scored 31 times in 11 Serie A games. In the past 65 years only two Italian teams – the Juventus and Napoli sides of 2017-18 – had made a more prolific start to a top-flight campaign. More importantly, Roma’s victory meant they remained undefeated in domestic competition this season. Just like their neighbours Lazio, who drew 1-1 away against Napoli in the early kick-off on Sunday. Continue reading...

item.title: Felix Nmecha’s faith is forcing Borussia Dortmund into an uncomfortable debate | Andy Brassell
item.description: Midfielder’s spectacular strikes rescued a frustrating day, only for celebrations to reignite dialogue that has followed him through his career It was just what they needed at just the right time. For a tricky first half and beyond, Elversberg had been a stone in Borussia Dortmund’s shoe, the promoted side not just keeping the home team at bay but keeping them honest, nourishing ambitions of their own. “The fatigue was clearly visible,” the sporting director, Ole Book, said to Sky after a week which had contained Der Klassiker in Munich and a hard-fought Champions League victory against Betis. “We were a bit too focused on managing the game, which was understandable.” Enter Felix Nmecha. BVB have enjoyed a largely excellent start to the season, are unbeaten and level on points with Bayern Munich at the top; Bayern lead, unsurprisingly, thanks to their superior goal difference. It is a gap which has been widened by Dortmund being far from prolific, a facet which looked as if it might undercut their efforts to roll over their visitors on Saturday, especially in the absence of the injured centre-forward Serhou Guirassy. Continue reading...

item.title: Lens were humiliated by Como. The pain continued against Marseille
item.description: Pierre Sage led Lens to second and glory in the Coupe de France last season. A lot has changed in the last six months The Lens striker, Florian Sotoca, was completely motionless as he looked into the middle space from the bench. The game, finely poised at 2-1 with a few minutes remaining, was not beyond his side, but that is not the story his troubled face told. Marseille had just restored their lead thanks to a goal from substitute Keyliane Abdallah. Bruno Génésio’s men would go on to take all three points and continue their unlikely charge up the table, but the atmosphere at the Stade Bollaert-Delelis was morose before Marseille had even stepped on the pitch. The match did little to lift the mood at the end of a week in which Lens made unwanted history. Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: Tullis-Joyce takes charge and is Shaw the perfect striker?
item.description: The City forward hit a WSL hat-trick for the ninth time while Eva Olid’s United have found defensive stability Not only did Khadija “Bunny” Shaw score a record-extending ninth WSL hat-trick, she scored a “perfect hat-trick” for the fourth time in the competition, something nobody else has managed more than once. Against West Ham the Jamaica striker opened the scoring with her left foot, headed home her second off the underside of the crossbar and tucked in her third with her right foot late on. It helped her side towards a 5-0 win that opened up a two-point gap at the top of the table and stretched Shaw’s lead in the race to be the top division’s top scorer to a five-goal advantage over her nearest challenger, Océane Hurtré. Can anybody stop her relentless pursuit of another Golden Boot? It would appear not. Tom Garry Match report: Liverpool 1-2 Arsenal Continue reading...

item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Delap’s talents resurface in style, Gómez delights Brighton with more fireworks, and hair-pulling confusion at Everton It would have been very easy for Oliver Glasner to lose patience with Liam Delap. The forward is still only 23, yet the days when he was rattling in 12 in a Premier League season for Ipswich have come to seem a very long time ago (and his six games for Manchester City even longer). A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. Jonathan Wilson Match report: Nottingham Forest 3-1 Manchester City Match report: Manchester United 4-4 Aston Villa Match report: Brighton 2-0 Brentford Match report: Arsenal 1-0 Hull Match report: Sunderland 1-0 Chelsea Match report: Leeds 1-0 Tottenham Continue reading...

item.description: The stand-in left-back has become a pantomime villain but United fans are understandably struggling to focus their ire Sporting success is, supposedly, a nigh-on irrelevance to Manchester United’s global brand. The money will stream in regardless thanks to the behemoth company it has become, leaving behind its football club roots and becoming the world’s greatest soap opera creating the sort of drama of which Phil Mitchell can only dream. There is a strong cast of characters from the hated billionaire owners to the under‑pressure manager and pantomime villain Diogo Dalot, and a collection of storylines that are becoming hard to believe. Amid the supervillains, there are the unmistakable petty culprits who have brought United down to 18th place in the Premier League and Michael Carrick wondering how much longer he can survive. Continue reading...

item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

item.title: ‘In moments of pain, football comes together’: Spain says goodbye to Jesús de Miguel
item.description: Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but the streets of Navahermosa were fuller yet quieter to mourn the Tenerife striker at his funeral The narrow streets of Navahermosa in La Mancha were fuller than they have ever been on Thursday afternoon and quieter too. Silence accompanied the funeral cortege as its made way from the funeral home to the parish church of San Miguel Arcángel carrying Jesús de Miguel Alameda, “Demi”, the Tenerife striker who died after an on-field collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono three days earlier. Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but now they were joined by the game he loved. “We wanted to be close to his parents, his wife and daughter. In moments of pain, football comes together more than ever,” said Luis de la Fuente. The Spain manager did not say much else; there was not much else he could say, not much anyone could. These have been dark, desperate days, days when it was impossible to assimilate what has happened, and there will be more. “We will get through this together but we will need help, professional help,” the Tenerife president, Felipe Miñambres, said. Continue reading...

Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but now they were joined by the game he loved. “We wanted to be close to his parents, his wife and daughter. In moments of pain, football comes together more than ever,” said Luis de la Fuente. The Spain manager did not say much else; there was not much else he could say, not much anyone could. These have been dark, desperate days, days when it was impossible to assimilate what has happened, and there will be more. “We will get through this together but we will need help, professional help,” the Tenerife president, Felipe Miñambres, said. Continue reading...

item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo merely the latest example of a great player who couldn’t let go | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There is no doubt his international career was an incredible one, but it would have been greater still if he had not lingered on the stage so long Nothing, perhaps, is quite so difficult for an elite sportsperson as timing their exit. It’s not easy for any person in any job to weigh the hope of having more to give with the desire not to linger beyond their usefulness, but it’s perhaps particularly hard for top athletes because unrealistic self-confidence is so essential to their success. It takes an almost unhealthy level of self-belief for anybody to make the sacrifices to get to the top, to dedicate themselves to such a precarious vocation, to overcome all the setbacks and injuries and failures. How can someone – whose whole life has been spent assuring themselves there are no odds they cannot overcome – accept that is it, that the time has come to say goodbye? The news that Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football brings with it, inevitably, a sadness. Sadness we will no longer see him skipping past a defender, or burying a neck-thrusting header, and sadness in that the end of the career of any great is a reminder of mortality; all things in time must pass. But there is also a sadness he timed his departure so badly. For at least three tournaments, there has been a sense of Ronaldo holding Portugal back. Continue reading...

item.title: Billions in revenue proves Fifa right on the World Cup – but only on things it cares about
item.description: The 2026 edition of the tournament brought in untold amounts of money to Gianni Infantino’s governing body The total hasn’t entirely stopped rising yet, still clicking away towards a final tally. Still, Fifa has already announced that it surpassed its own lofty revenue projections for the 2026 World Cup, bringing in $15bn, significantly more than anticipated. It appears that a third of that total – $5bn – came from ticket sales and hospitality alone, per reporting from the Times . That would mean direct income from the matchgoing fans came in five times as high in the United States, Canada and Mexico as it did at the last World Cup, in Qatar in 2022, when the total stood at $929m. While 2026’s expanded World Cup added 40 games to the schedule, the takings nevertheless went from an average of about $14.5m per match to about $48m. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘She can do what Beckham did’: Océane Hurtré making waves at Birmingham
item.description: WSL’s second-highest goalscorer is likened to England legend for her crossing and has earned France call-up At the conclusion of Birmingham’s warm-up, the players quietly and carefully placed their footballs into a draw-string bag. All except one, Océane Hurtré, who nonchalantly chipped hers straight into the bag from about 15 yards. It was an innocuous moment that might have escaped most onlookers at Hednesford Town’s Keys Park but it demonstrated the swagger with which she is playing. To observe the 22-year-old warming up before the 1-1 League Cup draw at Aston Villa last week was to witness a player making skills look easy, taking one touch where others took two and pulling off no-look passes. She is backing up that panache in the Women’s Super League, as the joint second-highest goalscorer with six from the promoted side’s opening eight matches. Only Khadija Shaw has scored more. Continue reading...

item.title: Choke of the century? Chengdu collapse sets up thrilling Chinese Super League climax
item.description: John Aloisi’s players need a point on the final day to seal their maiden title – but their form has dropped off a cliff With four games of the Chinese Super League to go, Chengdu Rongcheng needed just a point to clinch their first title. With one game to go, they still need a point. What was a formality has become a formidable task. The biggest bottle job in Asian football history is very much on and it would be as popular as it would be dramatic. The coach of the Sichuan club, the former Portsmouth and Coventry striker John Aloisi, has seen a 12-point lead over Dalian Yingbo cut to just three before Sunday’s showdowns. Whatever happens, this is a positive and thrilling end to a season that started negatively – literally – with nine of the 16 top-tier clubs kicking off on minus points. Continue reading...

item.title: Has a footballer ever run a marathon faster than James Milner? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: managers sacked after signing new deals, war victims commemorated on kits and the first club website (part II) Mail us with all of your questions and answers It came as no surprise to the Knowledge that James Milner had spent the early months of his retirement training for – and then running in – the New York City Marathon. Yes, the bleep test-loving former Brighton, Liverpool and Manchester City player recorded an excellent time of 3hr 9min 4sec, an average of 7min 13sec per mile. Not bad for a 40-year-old whose physique is more like that of a wrestler than a whippet. “A few years ago, I feel like I could have definitely done sub-3:00,” he said, lamenting his late-career injuries for hindering him. In 2012 we ran a column listing footballers’ fastest marathon times, with the former Leicester playmaker Muzzy Izzet leading the pack on 3hr 22min 36sec at the 2011 London Marathon. That very respectable time has now been surpassed by the Premier League’s record appearance maker, so we thought we had better take a gulp of our isotonic energy drink and run through a few more tales of football’s marathon men and women. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘An absolute afterthought’: the story of the Nigeria women’s team’s fall from grace
item.description: The Super Falcons won’t be at the World Cup and with the prize money going up, they risk being left even further behind It was a historic result in Casablanca – but not in a good way. Nigeria’s 2-1 defeat against South Africa in a playoff in August meant that the Super Falcons are missing out on the World Cup for the first time. It is a crushing blow for the most decorated national side in Africa across both men and women, one that has won no fewer than 10 Wafcon titles . The journalist and lecturer Dr Victor Ademola was in Morocco the day of the defeat. “It was a very difficult evening,” he says. “Some players were visibly emotional while others appeared to be processing what had just happened. I saw players crying as they got on to the team bus while some sat alone or remained on their phones, looking very sad.” Continue reading...

item.title: From VHS dreams to San Siro glory: Amorim’s Milan surge puts rivals on notice | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Inspired by the legendary Milan sides of his youth, the manager gave his side a lift with a tactical victory over Inter Ruben Amorim had waited a lifetime for his first Milan derby. As a kid growing up in Lisbon, he supported two football teams. There was the local one, Benfica, whose games he attended so early in life that his father has recalled changing nappies in the stands of the old Estádio da Luz. And the other one that captivated him from overseas. “I remember watching tapes of that Milan team with [Paolo] Maldini, [Franco] Baresi, [Ruud] Gullit, [Frank] Rijkaard, [Dejan] Savicevic,” Amorim told the Portuguese newspaper Expresso in 2017. “My childhood dreams were to play for Benfica and Milan. I’ve fulfilled one. Now I suppose I’ll have to become a coach for the other!” Continue reading...

item.title: Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or party gives way to anxiety-filled hangover for Bayern Munich | Andy Brassell
item.description: Dortmund did not read the script, remaining level on points with the defending champions at the top of the table It was the moment they had all been … not so much waiting for, but planning, pushing and yearning for. In the videos that announce the starting lineup on the giant scoreboard before kick-off, every Bayern Munich player turns to face the camera with their personal salute, greeting or goal celebration, the playful progression from the standard folding of arms. Except on Saturday evening, the No 9 turned around smiling, and cradling the golden trophy. In the midweek DFB Pokal stroll against Magdeburg there had been a salute, the players welcoming Harry Kane on to the pitch with a guard of honour to commemorate his Ballon d’Or victory two nights before. This, however, was the real party, the moment where the England captain’s and Bayern’s successful union and the apex it has reached was celebrated in front of a global audience. There was every reason to believe it would be a full and satisfying victory lap, even in Der Klassiker, with proper competition so often bringing the best out of the Rekordmeister. Continue reading...

item.title: Folarin Balogun takes a first, tiny step toward moving on from a calamitous summer
item.description: The USMNT striker scored his first goal since the World Cup in a losing effort against Paris FC. Could it lead to something more? Before this weekend, the last time Folarin Balogun scored was in the United States’ 2-0 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina at this past summer’s World Cup. In the immediate aftermath, the outlook for Balogun seemed rosy; an ascendant player who could muster a goal in tense games. At half-time against Bosnia, US fans weren’t just wondering how far his team could advance – they were sizing Balogun up against some of the world’s best strikers. But for most of the ensuing four months, Balogun has been in limbo. His breakout World Cup was overshadowed by a red card in that same game against Bosnia and Herzegovina, followed by a scandal of which he wanted no part. Just as it seemed a summer move away from Monaco could get his club career on track, he broke off a possible deadline-day move to Everton after a lengthy visit to the training grounds and a medical he felt was improperly handled. Continue reading...

item.title: Rampant Salford hint that Beckham’s lofty ambitions are not a pipe dream
item.description: The aim of reaching the Championship looks more realistic for a Manchester club in the shadow of City and United After seven seasons in League Two, Salford City are finally threatening to match the hype brought by their high-profile owners. First it was the Class of ’92 who guided them up through the non-league system into the fourth tier but failed to progress any further. Gary Neville and David Beckham remain, part of a new group that took over in May 2025, with this year beginning to look transformational after securing an eighth straight win, against Exeter, to put them five points clear at the top. The budget has increased, allowing the club to sign a number of players who will feel they are above League Two standard. Striker Macaulay Langstaff arrived from Millwall; the last time he played at this level, he scored 28 league goals in a season for Notts County. Match-winner Will Aimson spent the past two seasons in the division above with Wigan and has dropped down because of Salford’s project. Continue reading...

item.title: How can playing for Manchester City fit into Marc Guéhi’s moral universe? | Barney Ronay
item.description: Club’s predicament raises interesting questions about principles, both for individuals and the Premier League I felt unbelievably ponderous. My head was made of Aztec stone. I realised I didn’t want to be with all these people. Somebody came at me, a huge individual in silver and blue. I fell at his feet and grabbed one shoe. I started untying the lace. He kicked away from me. I got up and walked off. I was exceedingly hungry. Not my words. Also not the words of the Manchester City centre-back Marc Guéhi, despite what you were thinking there. This is instead a condensed quote from the mind of Gary Harkness, existentially curious college running-back and the narrator of Don DeLillo’s great American football novel End Zone. Continue reading...

item.title: A phone-free Yellow Wall: are Dortmund urging fans to be present or policing them?
item.description: It makes sense that sports teams want to keep influencers out of their games. The battle some clubs are waging with their fans, however, is a different dilemma By all appearances, things on the Yellow Wall seemed as they always had been. The stadium announcer hollered out the first names of Borussia Dortmund’s starting lineup and the supporters responded with their last names, tens of thousands of voices bellowing as one. Dozens of black and yellow flags waved over Europe’s largest standing terrace, a mass of faces fixed on the field beneath them. And then Signal Iduna Park, sold out with 81,365 fans, roared when Max Beier’s lone goal led Dortmund to victory over Eintracht Frankfurt last Saturday, putting the home side even on points with Bayern Munich atop the Bundesliga standings. Continue reading...
